## WriteResultsBuffer

*源文件：`VisionTools/WriteResultsBuffer.htm`*

Writes data from a referenced Buffer data structure, created by a FormatOutputBuffer function, to the currently enabled factory communication protocol. This function also writes the Result Code field for the factory communication protocols.

### Inputs

The WriteResultsBuffer function has the following syntax: WriteResultsBuffer(Event, InspectionID, Buffer, Result Code, Protocol, Byte/Word Order) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Event | Specifies the event that forces an update. This parameter needs to refer to any event with a timestamp, for example, one of the following: <br>- A cell containing an Event function. <br>- A cell containing a Button function. |
| Inspection ID | If the function references a cell pointing to a PointCloud structure (default = A0), the Inspection ID of the result is the Acquisition ID of the hardware acquisition that produced the result, or -1=0xFFFF if the PointCloud does not come from a hardware acquisition. If the function references a cell with an integer value, the Inspection ID of the result is set to that value. Buffer Specifies a reference to a Buffer data structure created by a FormatOutputBuffer function, which contains automatically formatted data. Result Code Specifies an integer that can be used to communicate the result of the inspection to any connected devices. Protocol Specifies which protocol the user data needs to be written to. 1 = EtherNet/IP Specifies that EtherNet/IP is the enabled factory communication protocol. 2 = PROFINET Specifies that PROFINET is the enabled factory communication protocol. 3 = SLMP Protocol Scanner Specifies that SLMP is the enabled factory communication protocol. 4 = Modbus TCP Server Specifies that Modbus TCP is the enabled factory communication protocol. 100 = Default Specifies that the currently enabled factory communication protocol is used. If more than one protocol is enabled, the first enabled protocol is used. Byte/Word Order Specifies the bit order for words and bytes read by the function. 0 = Big endian Specifies that the most significant byte is stored first and subsequent bytes are stored in descending order. 1 = Little endian Specifies that the least significant byte is stored first and subsequent bytes are stored in ascending order. 2 = Big endian with 16-bit word swapping Big endian byte style is applied and double word types have their word pair order switched. (16-bit words) 3 = Little endian with 16-bit word swapping Little endian byte style is applied and double word types have their word pair order switched. (16-bit words) 100 = Default The default setting is used. |

### Outputs

Returns
A Write Result data structure containing the data sent to the client, or #ERR:

- If an input parameter is invalid
- If a connection to a client has not been established

## Color Components of a Pixel

*源文件：`VisionTools/colorcomponents.htm`*

In-Sight Spreadsheet color vision systems capture image data in the RGB color space. This image data is then stored in memory, and can be exported either to 24-bit Bitmap format, or to JPEG format. Based on data in one color space, the system can convert the acquisition mathematically to another color space. Some tools, such as ColorToGreyscaleFilter, take advantage of this explicitly, while others, such as monochrome 2D tools do this implicitly, where operating on a single color plane, or operating separately on color planes do not produce desirable results. By default, the available color 2D Vision Tools operate on the entirety of the acquired color image, and while different tools may use that data differently, all color information is used for results calculation. Each color pixel is composed of three separate color components. These components can be represented as combinations of red, green and blue (RGB), or hue, saturation and intensity (HSI HSI stands for hue, saturation, and intensity in the RGB color model.). For both RGB and HSI, each component of a pixel is converted to a value from 0 to 255. RGB colors are created by combining shades of red, green and blue in different proportions. The combination produces a specific color for each pixel; examples are shown below.

The values of the RGB components for the above 'pixel' are (255,0,0)
The values of the RGB components for the above 'pixel' are (0,255,0)
The values of the RGB components for the above 'pixel' are (0,0,255)
The values of the RGB components for the above 'pixel' are (200,0,0)
The values of the RGB components for the above 'pixel' are (150,0,0)
The values of the RGB components for the above 'pixel' are (85,0,0)
For HSI, the hue of a color corresponds to its location within the visible portion of the electromagnetic spectrum of radiation: The conversion of a hue to a numerical value is done by creating a color wheel. A color wheel places all of the hues from the spectrum on a circle. A particular hue is specified by giving the angle at which that hue lies on the color wheel. The following figure shows a color wheel: Note: The range of hue values is scaled to the range 0 through 255. The saturation of a color is the degree to which the color is mixed with grey or white. A fully saturated color is pure. As a color becomes mixed with white (or grey) it becomes less saturated. The following figure shows a range of saturation values for a single hue: The intensity of a color is a measure of its brightness. The intensity of a color is defined as the average value of the red, green and blue components that make up the color. The resulting mixture of hue, saturation and intensity produces the correct color for each pixel; examples are shown below.

The values of the HSI components for the above 'pixel' are (0,255,85)
The values of the HSI components for the above 'pixel' are (85,255,85)
The values of the HSI components for the above 'pixel' are (170,255,85)

## Spreadsheet Toolbox

*源文件：`VisionTools/insighttoolbox.htm`*

Vision applications are configured by inserting formulas into spreadsheet cells. These formulas are constructed using the functions available in the Spreadsheet Toolbox, which is available on the first tab of the panel on the right side of the user interface. Functions can be inserted into the spreadsheet cells by either:

- Dragging and dropping from the Toolbox.
- Selecting a cell and using the Insert Function dialog.
- Selecting a cell and typing the name of the function, followed by the "(" character. You can also insert a function by typing tool names, or parts of tool names into a cell or the Insert Function dialog and a pop-up box appears showing the names of the matching tools. For example, typing "patmax" into a cell shows both TrainPatmaxRedline and FindPatmaxRedline functions. If there is no matching tool name, the box disappears.

## Snippets Panel

*源文件：`VisionTools/snippet-dialog.htm`*

The Snippets panel allows you to automate frequently performed spreadsheet tasks by creating groups of pre-configured cells. To access the Snippets panel, choose Snippets from the View tab of the Menu Bar. From the Snippets panel, you can access common snippets provided by Cognex. You can access your own exported snippets in the Custom Snippets folder. When you drag and drop a Cognex snippet A snippet is one or more pre-configured cell that allows you to automate frequently performed spreadsheet tasks. You can create your own snippets, or use snippets provided by Cognex. into the spreadsheet, the top row shows a description of the snippet.

## Export Snippets

- Select the cell(s) with the data to export.
- From the File menu, click Export Snippet, or alternately, right-click on the cells with the data to export and select Snippets > Export Snippets from the shortcut menu. You can also use the hotkey ALT+E.
- Name the snippet file and click Save.

## Import Snippets

You can import snippets either through the file explorer or by dragging and dropping a snippet from the Snippets panel into the spreadsheet. To import from the file explorer:

- Select an empty cell.
- From the File menu, click Import Snippet, or alternately, right-click on the cell and select Snippets

> Import Snippets from the shortcut menu. You can also use the hotkey ALT+I.

- Select the snippet file and click Open.

## View Files Stored on the In-Sight Vision System

*源文件：`VisionTools/view-files-on-device.htm`*

View files stored on the vision system either using The File Management utility in In-Sight Vision Suite or a third-party FTP client, such as FileZilla Client. The FTP client must support TLS 1.3. Viewing files this way is useful if you use the WriteImage or WriteData function to write files to the internal storage of the vision system.

## View Files in In-Sight Vision Suite

To view files on the vision system:

- Launch In-Sight Vision Suite if it is not already running.
- Left-click the vision system you want to configure on the In-Sight® Device Pane on the left. The list of Utilities applicable to the selected vision system then appears at the bottom of the window.
- Click the File Management button. The utility dialog then opens.
- Browse the directory tree. Copy, move, or delete files as needed. For more information, see the In-Sight Vision Suite Help documentation.

## View Files Using FileZilla Client

To view files using FileZilla Client:

- Download FileZilla Client from filezilla-project.org and install it.
- Open FileZilla Client.
- Configure the following fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
|  | Host The host name or IP address of the vision system. You can find these details in In-Sight Vision Suite after you select a vision system. Username The user credentials of the vision system. <br>- The default username is admin. <br>- The default password is blank. Note: You can change the credentials using the User Settings utility. |
| Password | <br>- Click Quickconnect. <br>- You can now view the stored files. The Field Path field in In-Sight 3D Spreadsheet determines where the vision system saves the files. If you leave the File Path field blank, the files are saved to the root directory. |

## Create a Subfolder Using FileZilla Client

If you want to separate images from text files, create a folder structure on the vision system using FileZilla Client. The following example walks you through creating a subfolder Job1 under the Images directory:

- In FileZilla Client, right-click on the Images directory and select Create directory. The Create directory dialog appears.
- In the dialog, enter /Job1, then click OK. The Job1 subfolder is now available under the Images directory.
- In In-Sight 3D Spreadsheet, connect to the vision system.
- Enter Images/Job1 to the File Path field in the WriteImage property sheet, using forward slash as the folder separator.
- Click OK to close the property sheet.

Now the images are sent to the Job1 subfolder under the Images directory.

## How to Configure the WriteData Function

*源文件：`VisionTools/writedata-how-to.htm`*

The WriteData function allows you to write data to a file or append a data string to a file on a local device or an FTP/SFTP server. You can use this function to log data results and view them in a file. Note: You can save the file to the selected Storage location while Online or Offline. The following describes how to configure the WriteData function when connected to an In-Sight vision system:

- Connect to the In-Sight vision system.
- Insert the WriteData function into the spreadsheet, which opens the WriteData property sheet. Configure the following parameters, using the default settings for the rest of the parameters:
- Data: Enter a text string or a reference to a cell containing a text string you want to write or append to a file. In this example, the Data parameter references cell C0, which is configured as: Stringf("Test string.\r\n")
- File Name: Enter a File Name for your data file.
- After configuring the parameters, click OK to close the property sheet. The WriteData data structure is inserted to the spreadsheet.
- Trigger the vision system.
- A data file (In-Sight.txt) is stored on the In-Sight device, and within the file, "Text string." is written.
- If you trigger the vision system again, within the text file, another "Test string." is appended to the file.
- Use FTP software to view the files. For more information, see View Files Stored on the In-Sight Vision System.

Note:

- For more information on each parameter setting, see WriteData.
- If you want to send the files to an FTP/SFTP server, set Storage to FTP Server or SFTP Server, and enter the server address (Server), User Name and Password in the corresponding fields.

# 3D 视觉工具函数（3DVisionTools，共 169 页）

## 2D to 2D Conversion

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/2d-to-2d-conversion.htm`*

Example: Fixturing a 2D tool from a 2D Fixture. Steps:

- Train and find PatMaxRedLine or any other 2D fixturing function. This gives you the X, Y, and Angle values.
- Use ExtractCalibration tool on the A1 Image cell. This returns a calibration structure that you can reference in the TransWorldToPixel tool.
- Use the TransWorldToPixel tool.
- In the Calib field, enter the ExtractCalibration cell reference.
- For Point, enter the X and Y values created by FindPatMaxRedLine.
- Multiply the Angle value from FindPatMaxRedLine by -1.
- You can now use these X, Y (pixel), and Angle values as fixture for 2D tools like DetectBlobs, or Region, and measurement inputs for 2D tools such as PointToPoint or LineToLine.

## 3D Fixture Functions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_CoordinateTrans_Fixture.htm`*

The 3D Fixture functions allow you to construct fixtures in the 3D space, to be used by other 3D vision tools when configuring an inspection. The available functions allow you to create a fixture from a point, line, plane, or multiple structures as well.

## 3D Cross-Section Functions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_CrossSection_Tools.htm`*

The In-Sight 3D Cross-Section functions allow you to extract 2D cross-sections or profiles from a 3D point cloud along a Region of Interest. You can further analyze the geometric information provided by the 2D profile using Profile tools to verify that an object is defect-free and meets specifications. Applications include:

- Inspecting glue and weld seams
- Verifying component height
- Identifying surface defects
- Measuring gaps, diameters, or thickness

| 3D Point Cloud with Cross-Section Tool | Profile View |

The following functions are available in the 3D Cross-Section function group:

- ExtractCrossSection3D: Extracts a profile from a point cloud using the points that intersect with a user-defined 3D rectangle.
- ExtractParallelCrossSections3D: Extracts multiple parallel 2D profiles from a user-defined 3D Region of Interest within the point cloud.

For a list of Profile tools that you can use to further analyze extracted 2D profiles, see 3D Profile Functions.

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_Image.htm`*

The In-Sight 3D Image tool processes the input point cloud to enhance desirable features while removing or diminishing undesirable features; the result is an enhanced input image or a new output image that is better suited for additional data-extraction functions such as Blob or Histogram analysis.

## 3D Pattern Match Functions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_PatternMatch.htm`*

The In-Sight Spreadsheet Pattern Match functions are used to train and find 3D patterns with Cognex's proprietary PatMax3D® technology. These PatMax3D functions allow you to locate features in an input point cloud that exhibit maximum similarity to a trained 3D pattern. The process specifics of pattern finding may differ depending on the nature of the similarity metrics employed, but the basic concepts remain more or less the same regardless of the implementation. The pattern finding process consists of two phases: training and finding.

- In the training phase, a 3D Region of Interest (ROI) containing an example of the pattern to be located is manually identified and extracted to create a trained pattern.
- In the finding phase, new point cloud acquisitions presented to the system are searched for positions that exhibit maximum similarity, according to the specified metrics. These local match positions are sorted in order of descending similarity, and the best responses above a specified minimum level of similarity are then reported.

In-Sight Spreadsheetoffers the following high-speed and high-accuracy 3D pattern match tools:

- TrainPatMax3D: Extracts and trains a pattern from a point cloud. This pattern is then used by the FindPatMax3D function.
- FindPatMax3D: Finds matches to the 3D pattern trained with TrainPatMax3D.

## 3D Input/Output Functions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_PointCloud.htm`*

The 3D input/output functions allow you to add a new point cloud into the Spreadsheet Editor, load or save existing point cloud data, and access the acquisition settings of the vision system.

## 3D Profile Fixture Functions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_ProfileFixture_Tools.htm`*

The 3D Profile Fixture functions allow you to set up profile fixture coordinates that 3D profile feature extraction tools can use as input. Using a profile fixture ensures that the profile feature extraction tool extracts the same feature from a profile regardless of any changes in position during acquisition. The profile fixture coordinates are on the same plane as the profile, and relative to the profile origin based on an input profile feature. Note: 3D Profile Fixture Tools are only able to track movements on the plane of the the profile extraction rectangle. To track movements outside the profile extraction plane, you can use a 3D Fixture tool on the profile. 3D Profile Fixture functions require a Profile3D structure and one or more 3D structures as input. The following 3D Profile Fixture functions are available:

- ProfileFixtureFromPoint3D - creates profile fixture coordinates from a Point3D structure, allowing you to track acquisition translation along the Xp and Zp axes. The ProfileFixtureFromPoint3D function cannot compensate for rotation in the acquisition.
- ProfileFixtureFromTwoLines3D - creates profile fixture coordinates from the intersection point of two Line3D structures, allowing you to track acquisition translation along the Xp and Zp axes. The ProfileFixtureFromTwoLines3D function cannot compensate for rotation in the acquisition.
- ProfileFixtureFromTwoPoints3D - creates profile fixture coordinates using two Point3D structures, allowing you to track acquisition translation along the Xp and Zp axes, as well as rotation along the Yp-axis.

## 3D Profile Functions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_Profile_Tools.htm`*

The In-Sight Spreadsheet Profile functions allow you to extract features from a Profile3D structure, which is the result of a Cross-Section Tool and perform additional analysis using the extracted data. You can use the extracted profile features for applications such as:

- Inspecting glue and weld seams
- Verifying component height
- Identifying surface defects
- Measuring gaps, diameters, or thickness

3D Point Cloud with ProfileExtractCircle3D
Profile View
Profile feature extraction functions allow you to extract circles, points, and lines from a profile. Profile feature extraction functions require an External Profile input, for which you can reference the Profile3D output cell of a cross-section extraction function. The following profile feature extraction functions are available:

- ProfileExtractCircle3D: Extracts a Circle3D structure and associated parameters from a profile.
- ProfileExtractCorner3D: Extracts all found corners as Point3D structures with associated parameters from a profile.
- ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D: Extracts all points of an edge as Point3D structures from a profile.
- ProfileExtractLine3D: Extracts a Line3D structure and associated parameters from a profile based on an average of the points in the Region of Interest.
- ProfileExtractPoint3D: Extracts minimum, maximum, and average points on the X and Z axis as Point3D structures from a profile.
- ProfileExtractTangent3D: Extracts a tangent above or below the profile as a Line3D structure.

When you add any profile feature extraction functions, profile fixture functions, or profile measurement functions to the Spreadsheet, the first argument is A0 by default. You can change the argument to a cell that contains an extracted profile. Changing the default A0 cell means that the inputs and outputs from the changed tool are not displayed on the PointCloud view, but only on the defined Profile view.

## 3D Vision Tools

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_Tools_Overview.htm`*

The In-Sight Spreadsheet Vision Tools consist of functions used to process 3D shapes, configure fixturing and locate preconfigured 3D patterns. These functions allow you to:

- Extract and process various 3D structures (such as blobs, circles, edges, histograms, planes, etc.) from the acquired point cloud.
- Perform feature-based fixturing, that is create 3D fixtures from shapes to be used in detection inspections.
- Train and find 3D fixtures using 3D patterns.

You can insert 3D vision tools into the spreadsheet either by using functions from the Insert Function Dialog or by dragging and dropping them from the Toolbox.

Description
GetRotation(Angles3D)
Returns the tilt direction angle of the specified Angles3D structure in degrees. The angle is measured in the X-Y plane of the original reference coordinate system, and specifies the direction for the projection of the tilted Z-axis onto that plane.
GetTilt(Angles3D)
Returns the tilt angle of the Angles3D structure in degrees on the Z-axis.

## Blobs3D Vision Data Access Functions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_VDA_Functions_Blob3D.htm`*

This section lists the available 3D Vision Data Access functions that get values from a Blobs3D structure, created by an ExtractBlob3D, ExtractBlobFromCylinder3D, ExtractBlobFromSphere3D, or SortBlob3D function.

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| GetBoundingBox(Blobs3D, [Index]) | Returns the minimum area rectangle of the object projection as a Box3D structure. The projection of the object is onto the reference plane. After computing the minimum area rectangle of the box projection, the height is extended from the reference plane to include all points in the blob. Note: The top face of the bounding box is always parallel to the reference plane. GetCenterOfMass(Blobs3D, [Index]) Returns the center of mass of the blob with the specified index as a Point3D structure. GetHeight(Blobs3D, [Index]) Returns the height of the blob with the specified index. GetHeightHistogram(Blobs3D, [Index], [BinSize], [MinValue], [MaxValue]) Returns the height histogram data of the blob with the specified index as a Histogram3D structure. GetNFound(Blobs3D) Returns the number of blobs extracted by the function. GetNPoints(Blobs3D) Returns the number of points for the specified blob. GetPrincipalBoundingBox(Blobs3D, [Index]) GetPrincipalBoundingBox first computes the principal axes of the blob (also known as the principal axes of inertia). The principal axes of inertia represent the axes around which the object would naturally rotate. There are three axes and they define a coordinate system. Returns the axis-aligned bounding box for the computed principal axes as a Box3D structure. Note: The computation assumes uniform density between the top surface of the blob and the reference plane. Note: The principal axes are not necessarily the same as the sensor XYZ axes. Note: The resulting bounding box may not have a face that is parallel to the reference plane. GetType(Blobs3D, [Index]) Returns the blob type of the blob with the specified index in numeric data. GetTypeText(Blobs3D, [Index]) Returns the blob type of the blob with the specified index in text. GetVolume(Blobs3D, [Index]) Returns the volume of the blob with the specified index. |

## Histogram3D Vision Data Access Functions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_VDA_Functions_Histogram3D.htm`*

This section lists the available 3D Vision Data Access functions that get values from a Histogram3D structure. Note: Each of the following functions references a Histogram3D structure for the first parameter. Index (zero-based) determines which result of the 3D histogram you want to reference. If you do not specify the index, the index defaults to zero, meaning the function returns the first result. In case Low and High parameters are supported, you can specify the minimum and maximum values of the value range to check by the function.

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
|  | GetBinSize(Histogram3D) Returns the size of the histogram's bins. GetDataValueAtPercentile(Histogram3D, Percentile) Considering the samples counted in the bins of the histogram, the value corresponding to a given percentile level lies in some bin of the histogram. This function returns the center of that bin, along with a Boolean value indicating whether that value is valid or not. GetEndValueOfBins(Histogram3D) Returns the ending value of the bin sequence. GetFrequency(Histogram3D, [Index]) Returns the frequency of the specified bin. GetHead(Histogram3D, [Low], [High]) Returns the lowest bin-center value across all the bins (and within the value range if specified) whose bin has a non-zero frequency. GetMax(Histogram3D) Returns the value of the most prevalent 3D point that occurs in the specified 3D region of interest of the histogram function. GetMaxInPercentileRange(Histogram3D, [Low], [High]) Considering the samples counted in the bins of the histogram, the value corresponding to a given percentile level lies in some bin of the histogram. This function returns the maximum value of that bin (or within the specified value range), along with a Boolean value indicating whether that value is valid or not. GetMean(Histogram3D) Returns the mean value of the 3D points by summing up the grayscale values for all points in the 3D region of interest of the function, and then dividing by the count of 3D points in the same range. GetMin(Histogram3D) Returns the value of the least prevalent 3D point that occurs in the specified 3D region of interest of the histogram function. GetNumberofBins(Histogram3D) Returns the number of bins. GetStandardDeviation(Histogram3D, [Low], [High]) Returns the standard deviation of the 3D points within the 3D region of interest of the function. GetStartValueOfBins(Histogram3D) Returns the starting value of the bin sequence. GetSumOfFrequencies(Histogram3D, [Low], [High]) Returns the number of 3D points within the specified threshold range. <br>- In the Low Count column of the histogram function output, it returns the number of 3D points below the threshold (returned by the GetThreshold function). <br>- In the High Count column of the histogram function output, it returns the number of 3D points above the threshold (returned by the GetThreshold function). GetTail(Histogram3D, [Low], [High]) Returns the highest bin-center value across all the bins (and within the value range if specified) whose bin has a non-zero frequency. GetThreshold(Histogram3D) Computes an optimum histogram threshold that does a binary segmentation of all the histogram data. That way, GetThreshold specifies a threshold level that maximizes similarity between the 3D region of interest of the histogram function and all possible binary re-quantization. |

## PointCloud 3D Vision Data Access Functions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3D_VDA_Functions_PointCloud.htm`*

This topic In MQTT, a topic is a channel name where devices can publish messages, or can subscribe to for receiving messages. lists the available 3D Vision Data Access functions that get values directly from the acquired point cloud data.

## Using the Functions

Each of the following functions references a PointCloud structure for the first parameter. Use the index parameters as follows:

- Index1 (zero-based) determines which acquisition of the point cloud data you want to reference.
- If you do not specify the index, the index defaults to zero, meaning the function returns the first acquisition.
- In case of the GetX, GetY and GetZ functions, Index2 is an optional parameter when using edges.

## Function List

The following table describes the available functions:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
|  | GetCount(PointCloud) Returns the number of point cloud acquisitions. GetEncoderOverrun(PointCloud) Returns true if an encoder overrun occurred during acquisition. GetEncoderStats(PointCloud) Returns a chart of the time intervals between consecutive profiles in the point cloud. The time intervals are measured in milliseconds. Use this function when the vision system is in encoder mode to detect encoder signal issues. If motion speed is constant but the graph shows anomalies, the encoder signal might be noisy or unstable. Note: The function returns no data when loading point clouds acquired with In-Sight 3D Spreadsheet version 25.1.0 or earlier. The following example shows a slowdown at the beginning of the point cloud acquisition. The increased time between profiles indicates reduced motion speed. Anomalies appear near profile 700, followed by an acceleration around profile 1000, which decreases the time between profiles. The following example shows manual motion during acquisition. The time between encoder pulses varies significantly, which causes irregular spacing between profiles. The following example shows periodic fluctuations in time between profiles during acquisition. This behavior occurs when using a dual channel encoder and the Actual Y resolution is set equal to the encoder resolution. Depending on the accuracy of the encoder, minor positioning errors can cause small variations in timing between profiles. To avoid this behavior, set the Actual Y resolution to 4x the encoder resolution value on the Correction tab. GetGreyscale(Image) Returns the reference to the 2D greyscale image acquired by the vision system. GetMinProfileTime(PointCloud) Returns the shortest time between two consecutive point cloud profiles in milliseconds. Use this function when the vision system is in encoder mode to detect encoder signal issues. If motion speed is constant, the value should be close to GetScanTime divided by the number of acquired profiles. A shorter value can indicate noise on the encoder signal. GetROIMaxZ(PointCloud) Returns the maximum Z of the ROI of the point cloud acquisition. GetROIMinZ(PointCloud) Returns the minimum Z of the ROI of the point cloud acquisition. GetScanTime(PointCloud) Returns the time between the acquisition of the first laser profile and the acquisition of the last laser profile in milliseconds. In other words, the function returns the time the laser is on. GetX(PointCloud, [Index1], [Index2]) Returns the X-axis coordinate of the point cloud center point. Note: The Index2 parameter is valid only in case of edges (where it specifies an endpoint with the value of 0 or 1). |
| GetY(PointCloud, [Index1], [Index2]) | Returns the Y-axis coordinate of the point cloud center point. Note: The Index2 parameter is valid only in case of edges (where it specifies an endpoint with the value of 0 or 1). |

## 3D Robotics

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3d-robotics.htm`*

The 3D Robotics group of structure functions allow you to convert the position and rotation coordinates for robot poses into a number of different coordinate conventions. Different robot manufacturers expect different pose formats:

- Quaternions (for example: ABB) - Fixed-axis Euler XYZ (for example: FANUC, MITSUBISHI, Yaskawa) - Moving-axis Euler ZYZ (for example: Kawasaki) - Moving-axis Euler ZYX (for example: KUKA) - Rotation vector in radians (for example: Universal Robots) Without a controlled conversion framework, mismatched conventions can result in incorrect robot orientation, flipped coordinate frames, unit scaling errors, singularities, gimbal lock issues, or integration delays during commissioning. The 3D Robotics group of structure functions provides a robust framework for converting 3D data such as Fixture3D into the specific formats required by most robot manufacturers. By using the 3D Robotics structure functions, you can ensure that the spatial output of your vision system is immediately actionable by the robot without the need for complex, manual coordinate geometry calculations in the robot program. The 3D Robotics structure functions use the following logic:
- The Pose3DFormat function defines the rules of the pose, such as the rotation convention (Euler angles, Quaternions, or Matrices) and the units of measurement (millimeters vs. meters). The Pose3DFormat function contains the metadata but no coordinate data.
- The Pose3D function is the actual container for spatial information, and uses a Pose3DFormat structure as input, as well as specific numeric values to represent a unique location and orientation in 3D space.
- The Pose3DFromFixture3D function generates a Pose3D structure from an existing Fixture3D structure, using a Pose3DFormat function reference to define the coordinate conventions.

## Workflow

The integration process generally follows a three-step transformation:

- Acquisition : The 3D vision system generates a point cloud.
- Localization: In-Sight tools identify a part and create a Fixture3D structure.
- Conversion: Using the Pose3DFromFixture3D function, the Fixture3D structure is converted into a Pose3D structure based on the settings defined in the Pose3DFormat function, matching the specific Rotation Convention, Angle Unit, and Length Unit of your chosen robot manufacturer.

## Supported Robot Manufacturer Conventions

To simplify deployment, refer to the following table below for the standard conventions used by supported vendors:

- **Vendor**：Convention (Rotation Format)
- **Translation Unit**：Angle Unit
- **ABB**：Quaternion (Scalar-First)
- **mm**：Unitless
- **FANUC**：Euler XYZ (Fixed Axis)
- **mm**：Degrees
- **KUKA**：Euler ZYX (Moving Axis)
- **mm**：Degrees
- **Universal Robots**：Rotation Vector
- **mm**：Radians
- **Yaskawa**：Euler XYZ (Fixed Axis)
- **mm**：Degrees

Note: Some formats have strict constraints. For example, In-Sight native formats must use Millimeters and Degrees, while Matrix and Quaternion formats require the Angle Unit to be set to None.

## 3D to 2D Conversion

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/3d-to-2d-conversion.htm`*

Example: Fixturing a 2D tool from a 3D Fixture. Note: Use Fixture3D to fixture 2D tools only when all the movement is on the XY plane. Steps:

- Train and find PatMax3D or any other 3D fixturing function. This gives you the X, Y, and Rotation values.
- Use the ExtractCalibration tool on the A1 Image cell. This returns a calibration structure that you can reference in the TransWorldToPixel tool.
- Use the TransWorldToPixel tool.
- In the Calib field, enter the ExtractCalibration cell reference.
- For Point, enter the X and Y values created previously by FindPatMax3D.
- Multiply the Rotation value from FindPatMax3D by -1.
- You can now use these X, Y (pixel), and Angle values as fixture for 2D tools like DetectBlobs, or Region, and measurement inputs for 2D tools such as PointToPoint or LineToLine.

## ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d.htm`*

The ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d function allows you to modify the acquisition settings of the vision system. The function supports a subset of the settings in the Acquisition panel. When you change the settings using this function, the vision system immediately stops the ongoing acquisition to apply the new settings. When the vision system finishes the reconfiguration, it automatically resumes the acquisition. During the short time when the ongoing acquisition stops, the vision system discards all triggers and these triggers are not considered missed triggers. For this reason, Cognex recommends you to stop the production line when performing changes. If you have more than one ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d functions in the spreadsheet, the vision system uses only the last updated value. For this reason, Cognex recommends to have only one ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d function enabled at a time. The values of the field correction settings are temporary, and they do not affect the field correction values stored on the vision system. When you restart the vision system or change jobs, the original field correction value is restored. Additionally, when exporting the field correction to a file, the original field correction value is used instead of the value configured by the ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d function. To use the function:

- Drag and drop the ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d function to the selected cell or type ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d into the selected cell. The property sheet of the function then opens.
- Check the checkbox next to the parameter you want to add and set the desired value.
- Click OK to close the Property Sheet.
- You can add cell references to the spreadsheet for any of the parameters by dragging and dropping the selected parameter to a cell. The following elements appear in the spreadsheet:
- An ❒AcquisitionSettings data structure, acting as the setter for the selected parameter.
- A label for the selected parameter for easy identification.
- An edit control element to modify the value of the parameter from the spreadsheet.
- Note:
- The label and the edit control of the parameter are populated only when you drag and drop the parameter from the ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d property sheet to the spreadsheet. If you insert the ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d function using other methods (such as typing ApplyAcquisitionSettings3d in a cell without checking and drag-and-dropping any parameters listed in the Property Sheet), only the ❒AcquisitionSettings data structure is created.
- If you uncheck a parameter in the Property Sheet, the associated edit control on the spreadsheet no longer overwrites the value of the parameter in the Acquisition panel.

### Inputs

The settings parameters are grouped in the property sheet based on their position in the Acquisition panel.

### Trigger Settings

| Time Trigger Delay (ms) | For more information, see Trigger Settings. |

## Box3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/Box3D.htm`*

The Box3D function allows you to create a fixtured 3D box in the point cloud. It returns a Box3D structure containing the settings of the fixtured 3D box.

### Inputs

The Box3D function has the following syntax: Box3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Box3D,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Box3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle of the function's 3D box. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the box along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the box along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the box along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the box's in-plane rotation (in degrees) about the tool's Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the box's tilt angle (in degrees) from the tool's Fixture3D Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the box's direction of tilt (in degrees) from the tool's rotated Fixture3D X-axis, about the tool's Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Show Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Box3D data structure containing the constructed 3D box, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

ExternalPointN],Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters. Note: This function can accept a variable number of arguments. Therefore, the function does not have a Property Sheet. After drag-and-dropping from the Toolbox onto the spreadsheet, you must complete it manually according to the above syntax. ## CompRegion3DFromCompRegion2D

Auto Compute Z Range Enables or disables automatic Z range computing for the Region3D structure. ## CompareHistogram3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/CompareHistogram3D.htm`*

The CompareHistogram3D function is used to compare two 3D histograms (existing in the spreadsheet as Histogram3D structures) in terms of their distribution of frequencies. When using the function, consider the following factors:

- To make sense of the comparison, Cognex recommends to compare histograms with similar configuration parameters (such as similar Bin and Subsample Sizes, or similar Minimum and Maximum values). Otherwise, the comparison percentage returned by the function will not reflect the similarity of the two object surfaces associated with the compared histograms.
- Regardless of the configured Bin Size, the number of bins must be the same in the compared histograms. If the number of bins are different, the function returns the Different Number of Bins error message.

### Inputs

The CompareHistogram3D function has the following syntax: CompareHistogram3D(PointCloud,ExternalHistogram0,ExternalHistogram1) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| External Histogram 1 | Specifies a reference to the second Histogram3D structure created in another cell to be used for comparison. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| External Histogram 0 | Specifies a reference to the first Histogram3D structure created in another cell to be used for comparison. |

### Outputs

Returns

The similarity percentage of the compared histograms, as an integer.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the function either returns an integer with a value range of 0 – 100 (standing for the similarity percentage), or #ERR if the function encountered any issues (such as a different number of bins in the two histograms).

## ComposeFixtures3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ComposeFixtures3D.htm`*

The ComposeFixtures3D tool allows you to integrate the fixturing coordinates of the robot and the vision system, in other words the tool is for calculating robot hand-eye coordination. It returns a ComposeFixtures3D structure containing the configured fixture coordinates.

### ComposeFixtures3D Inputs

The ComposeFixtures3D function has the following syntax: ComposeFixtures3D(FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D,Fixture3D)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D | Performs the correlation between the vision system and the robot. The FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D tool requires as inputs at least three points from the vision system and three points from the robot. The format is the following: FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D(vision system_Point1, vision system_Point2, vision system_Point3,..., vision system_PointN, Robot_Point1, Robot_Point2, Robot_Point3,..., Robot_PointN) |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |

### ComposeFixtures3D Outputs

Returns

A Fixture3D structure containing the parameters of the configured fixture coordinates, or #ERR if any parameter has been configured incorrectly.

Results

## Create2dHeightMapFromPointCloud

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/Create2dHeightMapFromPointCloud.htm`*

The Create2dHeightMapFromPointCloud function allows you to create a relative height map of all points within a Region of Interest (RoI) in the point cloud. The height map translates the relative height of each point in the RoI to a greyscale value between 0 and 255, allowing you to visualize the differences in height between the points. The function returns an Image structure containing a 2D height map image. The Create2dHeightMapFromPointCloud function is particularly useful in OCR applications, as it is capable of clearly highlighting the small features of embossed or engraved characters.

| Input Point Cloud

| | Output Height Map |

### Inputs

The Create2dHeightMapFromPointCloud function has the following syntax: Create2dHeightMapFromPointCloud(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Region3D,ExternalRegion,FeatureWidth,FeatureHeight,ProjectionMode,AutoAdjustBoxZRange,MatchInputResolution,RequestedPixelResolutionX,RequestedPixelResolutionY,DefaultMissingPixelHeight,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Match Grey Image Size | Match the height map image size to the greyscale image size. |
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Box3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the 3D rectangle of the function. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the box along the X-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeY The size of the box along the Y-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeZ The size of the box along the Z-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation of the box (in degrees) about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle of the box (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the tilt direction of the box (in degrees) from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Box is set to 0. |
| External Box | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Projection Mode | Specifies the method of calculating the relative height of the points in the point cloud. The available values are the following: <br>- Flex Inspect <br>- calculates the height of points relative to the surrounding points in the point cloud. This setting is useful when extracting characters on an uneven surface. <br>- Plane Inspect <br>- calculates the height of points relative to a local plane using the surrounding planar points in the point cloud. This setting is useful when extracting characters on a flat surface, such as VIN characters on an engine block. <br>- Curve Inspect <br>- calculates the height of points relative to a curved surface. The function calculates an expected curve from the point cloud data, using that curve as a reference for point height calculation. This setting is useful when extracting characters on a curved surface, such as characters on a tire for TireDOT reading. <br>- Height Map <br>- calculates the height of points relative to the bottom plane of the Region of Interest. |
| Feature Width | Specifies the expected width in millimeters of a typical feature of interest. The Feature Width parameter defines the resolution of the height map. Note: For OCR applications, the character stroke width defines the Feature Width setting. For example, if the character stroke is 1 mm, set the Feature Width to at least 0.25 mm in order to get good character resolution in the height map. Feature Height Specifies the expected height in millimeters of a typical feature of interest. The Feature Height parameter defines the sensitivity of the height map. Auto Adjust Box Z Range Specifies whether to automatically adjust the Z range of the RoI box to start with the height of the lowest point. This setting only applies when using Bottom of Region as the value for Projection Mode. Match Input Resolution Specifies whether to match the height map pixel size to the native resolution of the point cloud. Enabling this setting disables the Requested Pixel Resolution X and Requested Pixel Resolution Y settings. Requested Pixel Resolution X Specifies the number of pixels corresponding to the Feature Width value on the X axis. For example, if Feature Width is defined as 1 mm, and Requested Pixel Resolution X is defined as 5, then the output height map will have 5 pixels for 1 mm on the X axis. Note: If you change the value for Requested Pixel Resolution X, make sure to adjust the Requested Pixel Resolution Y parameter as well. Otherwise, the aspect ratio of the image is distorted. |
| Requested Pixel Resolution Y | Specifies the number of pixels corresponding to the Feature Width value on the Y axis. For example, if Feature Width is defined as 1 mm, and Requested Pixel Resolution Y is defined as 5, then the output height map will have 5 pixels for 1 mm on the Y axis. Note: If you change the value for Requested Pixel Resolution Y, make sure to adjust the Requested Pixel Resolution X parameter as well. Otherwise, the aspect ratio of the image is distorted. Default Missing Pixel Value Specifies the default height map value for pixels without any point cloud data. For example, if the Default Missing Pixel Value is 0, any pixels that do not contain point cloud data are shown as black. Height Mode Specifies whether the height map pixel value represents the Average, Minimum, or Maximum point value. Show Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

The Create2dHeightMapFromPointCloud function returns an Image structure containing a 2D height map image.

### How to convert 2D height map images to pixel coordinates

The Create2DHeightMapFromPointCloud function can produce inconsistent results depending on whether the Tilt input parameter takes a zero or non-zero value. If the Tilt value is 0, the function returns a calibrated image. Otherwise, the image is uncalibrated and operates in pixel coordinates. Use the CalibrateImage function that references the 2D height map image with a 0 value for the Calib parameter to convert calibrated images to pixel coordinates. Uncalibrated images are unaffected. This way, CalibrateImage always returns an uncalibrated image, which operates in pixel coordinates. Converting calibrated images to pixel coordinates ensures that the results are consistent when you use another 2D function with the 2D height map image. The following example and image demonstrates how to use the CalibrateImage function:

- The B3 cell contains a 2D height map created from the Point Cloud in A0.
- The B5 cell contains: CalibrateImage(B3,0) - The B8 cell contains a DetectBlobs function that references the B5 cell with the uncalibrated image.
- The B12 cell contains a DetectBlobs function that references the B3 cell with the 2D height map image that can be either calibrated or uncalibrated.
- The area of the blobs that reference the B5 cell with the CalibrateImage function are always in pixel coordinates. These are in the F8 and F9 cells.
- The area of the blobs that reference the B3 cell are either in pixel coordinates or calibrated world coordinates, depending on the Tilt of the Box3D parameter of the 2D height map image. These are in the F12 and F13 cells. Note: If you want to transform 2D regions to 3D regions from a 2D height map image, ensure that the Tilt value is 0. You can only create 3D regions from calibrated images.

Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. ## EdgeAIClassify3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/EdgeAIClassify3D.htm`*

The EdgeAIClassify3D function automatically classifies point cloud projection images into the defined classes based on an initial training image set. To use this function, you must define the classes, load an initial set of point clouds into the function, and then individually label a subset of the training images to ensure that the function recognizes the features on the projection images and classifies them correctly. Note: In earlier releases, Edge AI tools appeared under the name ViDi EL. Version 26.1.0 updates the user interface to the new naming. The following example shows how the function classifies objects in a point cloud. The input image contains a point cloud of croissants arranged on a tray. The output image shows the croissants classified into different classes based on their features.

| Input Point Cloud | Output Point Cloud |

## Getting Started

For a visual overview of the setup and training process, watch the video on using the EdgeAIClassify3D function on the Cognex Support Youtube channel.

## Using EdgeAIClassify3D

To use the EdgeAIClassify3D function:

- Drag and drop the EdgeAIClassify3D function into the Spreadsheet. The property sheet pops up: -

### Set up the Region of Interest (ROI).

Use any of the following methods:

- Double-click the Box3D parameter to set up the ROI in the acquisition display.
- Expand the Box3D parameter and define the box parameters manually.
- Double-click the External Box parameter and select a Box3D function cell in Spreadsheet.
- If the part tends to move in the scanning region, set up a fixture using the Fixture3D parameter.
- In the General tab, set the Projection Image Resolution in a way that makes the feature of interest easy to see. The feature of interest is the defect or any feature that you want the function to classify.
- In the Projection tab of the property sheet, select the Projection Mode, Feature Width, and Feature Height that you want the function to use for training. For more information, see Projection Parameters. Note: Click OK to apply the changes. This closes the property sheet. Open the property sheet again to see the training images with the updated projection mode in the Train and Images tabs of the property sheet.
- In the Train tab of the property sheet, add the classes you want the function to use.
- Click OK to close the property sheet.
- In the Spreadsheet, check the checkbox in the Collect Samples cell of the function. This allows the function to load images for training.
- Load images into the function either by double-clicking the desired images in the Filmstrip, or by clicking the Play button in the Filmstrip controls to load all of the images in the Filmstrip.
- Once you have loaded the training images, uncheck the checkbox in the Collect Samples cell of the function.
- Double-click the EdgeAIClassify3D cell in the Spreadsheet to re-open the property sheet. -

### Label at least five images for each class.

Use any of the following methods:

- In the Train tab, label the images one-by-one according to the desired class.
- In the Images tab, label multiple images at the same time:
- Press Ctrl and click to select multiple images.
- Drag and drop the images into the Labeled Images column of the desired class. Note: Once you have started labeling, you cannot change the ROI. -

### Review the Model Health indicator at the top of the table to check the performance of the function.

- The Model Health indicates how confident the function is in predicting the class of new, unseen images. Labeling images increases the Model Health percentage. Higher percentages indicate greater confidence.
- When you collect more images from the Filmstrip, the function starts to predict the class of unlabeled images.
- Continue labeling images until the Model Health is sufficiently high. Aim for 100%, if possible, but it might be difficult if you have highly variable images. You must decide what Model Health is acceptable for your specific application. Tip: Add new images to the Filmstrip during labeling to validate how accurately the function predicts classes.
- Optional: After labeling, click the Auto-Tune button in the Projection tab to automatically select the best projection settings for your application. For more information, see Auto-Tune option in Projection Parameters. Note: The selected projection mode is not visible in the property sheet until you close and reopen the property sheet.
- Click OK to finalize the function settings.

### Inputs

| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| Show | Select the type of graphic to overlay on the image. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Box3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the 3D rectangle of the function. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the box along the X-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeY The size of the box along the Y-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeZ The size of the box along the Z-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation of the box (in degrees) about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle of the box (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the tilt direction of the box (in degrees) from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Box is set to 0. |
| External Box | Specifies a reference to a Box3D structure defined in another cell to be used with the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function. |
| Projection Image Resolution | Specifies the resolution of the 2D projection image generated from the 3D point cloud within the ROI. The resolution determines the level of detail in the 2D projection image. This parameter affects tool performance in the following ways: <br>- Higher resolution captures finer surface details. <br>- The right resolution improves accuracy by better representing relevant features. <br>- Higher resolution requires more processing time, and it might be unsuitable for fast-moving production lines. The following settings are available: <br>- Low: Generates low-resolution images. Suitable for large, simple features or when speed is more important than detail. <br>- Medium: Balances detail and speed. Recommended for most use cases. <br>- High: Generates a high-resolution image. Best for detecting small features but can increase processing time. Each setting doubles the image resolution of the previous level. These are fixed resolution levels. Collect Samples Enables or disables sample collection for training. Unclassified Detection Enables or disables detection of unclassified results. When enabled, flags images that do not meet the confidence threshold for any defined class. Confidence Threshold Specifies the minimum confidence score for valid classification. The available range is 0–100. The default value is 70. A higher threshold results in stricter class assignment. |

### Projection Parameters

Projection is the process of converting 3D point cloud data into a 2D projection image. This is necessary because the tool works on 2D images, not raw 3D point cloud data. The tool uses different projection modes to transform point clouds into projection images. Each mode highlights specific types of features or surface characteristics. Choosing the right projection is important because it determines how features are visualized in the projection image. See the following examples:

- Use Height Map for flat surfaces with height differences.
- Use Shape Change for detecting edges.
- Use Flex Inspect for inspecting small defects on smooth surfaces. The Feature Width and Feature Height parameters determine the scale of the feature of interest used when generating the projection image. A low value for these parameters makes fine features more visible in the projection image. A high value smooths out fine features and makes coarse features more visible. These parameters do not apply equally to all projection modes. The following table summarizes which parameters apply to which projection mode: | Projecti

## EdgeAISegment3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/EdgeAISegment3D.htm`*

You can use the EdgeAISegment3D function for finding flaws or locating features on a 2D projection of a 3D image. You can create classes for the different features, so the function can search for several features at the same time. After training, the function can predict the appearance of the features in the new images. Note: In earlier releases, Edge AI tools appeared under the name ViDi EL. Version 26.1.0 updates the user interface to the new naming. The following example shows how the function finds flaws on objects in a point cloud. The input image shows a point cloud of an electric vehicle battery. The output image shows the battery, with its flaws classified into different classes based on their features.

| Input Point Cloud | Output Point Cloud |

Note: When using high-resolution images, the function can produce exceedingly small defect labels and can clutter the training due to the level of detail. You might need to zoom in to see these labels. You can either partially erase the labels on the images, or completely clear the entire label prediction to manage the detailed predictions.

## Getting Started

For a visual overview of the setup and training process, watch the video on using the EdgeAISegment3D function on the Cognex Support Youtube channel.

## Using EdgeAISegment3D

To add the EdgeAISegment3D function:

- Drag and drop the EdgeAISegment3D function into the Spreadsheet. The property sheet pops up: Note: If you are editing a EdgeAISegment3D function that has already been trained in an existing job, the function automatically shows predictions based on the training the function received. -

### Set up the Region of Interest (ROI).

Use any of the following methods:

- Double-click the Box3D parameter to set up the ROI in the acquisition display.
- Expand the Box3D parameter and define the box parameters manually.
- Double-click the External Box parameter and select a Box3D function cell in Spreadsheet.
- If the part tends to move in the scanning region, set up a fixture using the Fixture3D parameter.
- In the General tab, set the Projection Image Resolution in a way that makes the feature of interest easy to see. The feature of interest is the defect or any feature that you want the function to classify.
- In the Projection tab of the property sheet, select the Projection Mode, Feature Width, and Feature Height that you want the function to use for creating the image projections. For more information, see Projection Parameters. Note: If you change the Projection Mode after you already trained some images, the function adjusts all the images in the database to that projection as well.
- Start labeling images. Note: Once you have started labeling, you cannot change the ROI and projection settings. You can do the labeling in the following ways:
- Use the Pen tool by holding down the left mouse button to color the areas you want to mark.
- Use the Polygon tool by clicking around the edge of an area or feature to draw lines. Double-clicking closes up the lines and creates a colored polygon for you. If you do not like the label you created, you can use the Undo and Redo buttons, delete part of the markings with the Eraser tool, or all of them with the Clear button. The Clear button deletes every label in the image, regardless of the class. You can rename the class or give the class a new color by clicking on the Edit Class button.
- Click Accept Labels to train the image.
- Optional: After labeling, click the Auto-Tune button in the Projection tab to automatically select the best projection settings for your application. For more information, see the Auto-Tune option in Projection Parameters. Note: The selected projection mode is not visible in the property sheet until you close and reopen the property sheet.
- Click Next Image. At this point, the function makes a prediction, meaning that the function tries to find the patterns that you marked in the previous images.
- Fine-tune your labeling if needed. For example, there can be false predictions in your image. You can delete these faults by using the Eraser tool before accepting the changes.
- If needed, create more classes by clicking the Add Class button. You can have up to three classes defined. Name your new class and pick a different color. Note: Cognex recommends that you label at least five images for each class. The more images you train, the higher the quality of your output is. You can view your trained images in the sample viewer. To reach the sample viewer window, click the Edit button on the right. In the sample viewer, you can correct and finetune the trained images by clicking on the Edit button. You can also delete them by clicking on the Delete button, or you can edit the classes. Click the Edit Classes button to open the class editor where you can rename and delete classes, or change the class color:
- Click OK, if you finished labeling. The output of the function appears on the Spreadsheet.

## EditBox3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/EditBox3D.htm`*

The EditBox3D function inserts an interactive graphical Box3D control into the selected spreadsheet cell. It returns an EditBox3D control element, allowing you to modify the Box3D structure in accordance with the enabled parameters.

### Inputs

The EditBox3D function has the following syntax: EditBox3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Move,Size,Rotate,Name,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Move | Disables or enables the ability to adjust the input region position. This setting is enabled by default. |
| Size | Disables or enables the ability to resize the input region (that is, change its height and width). This setting is enabled by default. Rotate Disables or enables the ability to adjust the input region orientation. This setting is enabled by default. Name Specifies the text string label of the control. Show Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
