## ExtractBlob3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractBlob3D.htm`*

The ExtractBlob3D function is used to extract the blob (s) relative to a reference Plane3D structure. It returns the extracted blob(s) as a Blobs3D structure, which can be referenced with Blobs3D Vision Data Access functions.

### Inputs

The ExtractBlob3D function has the following syntax: ExtractBlob3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Region3D,ExternalRegion,PlaneFromRegion,Plane3D,ExternalPlane,AutoConnectivityDist,ConnectivityDist,AutoNoiseThreshold,NoiseThreshold,NumberToExtract,MinimumVolume,MaximumVolume,MinimumHeight,MaximumHeight,BlobTypes,SortKey,SortOrder,SortTolerance,SortReference,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Plane From Region | When checked, the function uses a plane derived from the configured Region3D region or External Region This is useful if you need only just a rough reference shape or surface, and you do not want to extract or explicitly define a plane. The setting is disabled (unchecked) by default. Note: Enabling this setting disables the Plane3D setting. |
| Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. Note: You can use Plane3D to mask data for training. The Plane3D function prevents the tool from taking any points that belong to that plane and are within the ROI. Note: This parameter is available only if the Plane from Region parameter is disabled, and the External Plane parameter is set to a value other than 0. |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. Note: This parameter is available only if the Plane from Region parameter is disabled. |
| Auto Connectivity Dist | When checked, the function automatically tries to estimate the smallest distance that two points can be apart, but still be considered to belong to the same blob result. This is achieved by using the known point cloud and sensor sampling distance. This parameter is enabled by default. Note: If the computed distance turns out to be smaller than the distance required for your specific inspection, regions in multiple blobs may become broken. In such cases, disable this setting and increase the connectivity distance manually with the Connectivity Distance parameter. Disable this setting to configure the connectivity distance manually. |
| Connectivity Distance | Specifies the maximum distance (in real-world units) between two points at which they are still considered to be part of the same blob. The value range is between 0.010 – inf., and default value is 1.0. Tip: Higher values connect points further apart. For example, if you see a region split in two blobs when you expected just one, increase the value of this attribute so that points further away are connected into same blob. Note: This parameter is enabled only if Auto Connectivity Dist is disabled. |
| Auto Noise Threshold | When checked, the function automatically sets the noise threshold of the blobs to be detected, based on the detected point cloud sampling distance. This parameter is enabled by default. Note: If the configured noise threshold turns out to be incorrect for your inspection, uncheck this attribute and configure the noise threshold manually with the following attribute. |
| Noise Threshold | Specifies the noise threshold of the blobs to be detected (in real-world units). This parameter creates a margin above and below the reference shape, and all points within this region are considered overlapping the reference shape. These points will not be part of any Positive or Negative blob types: only Unchanged blobs will contain them. Configuring this parameter properly helps you to deal with noisy points near the reference shape without affecting blob height and volume measurements. Tip: For most scenarios, Cognex recommends to set the Noise Threshold to the same value (or double that) of the Separation Distance Z-value. Larger values may also work for your inspection depending on the circumstances, as long as they do not exceed the minimum expected blob height. The value range is from 0 to inf., and the default value is 0. Note: This parameter is enabled only if Auto Noise Threshold is disabled. |
| Number to Extract | Specifies the maximum number of blobs to extract. The value range is 1 to 65535, and the default value is 1. |
| Minimum Volume | Specifies the minimum volume (in real-world units) that the blobs must have to be detected and included, allowing you to skip very small blobs that are probably caused by noise. The value range is from 0 to the configured value of the Maximum Volume property. The default value is 20). Tip: Cognex recommends setting this property as tight as possible to remove all unwanted blobs from the inspection. Maximum Volume Specifies the maximum volume (in real-world units) that the blobs can have to be detected and included, allowing you to keep large blobs that must be part of the inspection. The value range is from the configured value of the Minimum Volume property to inf. The default value is 100,000,000). Minimum Height Specifies the minimum height (in real-world units) that the blobs must have to be detected and included, allowing you to skip very small blobs that are probably caused by noise. The value range is from 0 to the configured value of the Maximum Height property. The default value is 1). Maximum Height Specifies the maximum height (in real-world units) that the blobs can have to be detected and included. The value range is from the configured value of the Minimum Height property to inf. The default value is 10000). Blob Types Specifies the blob types to detect or ignore by checking or unchecking their respective properties. The available types are the following: <br>- Positive: Specifies a positive volume with respect to the reference shape (that is a blob above the reference shape). This is the default setting. <br>- Negative: Specifies a negative volume with respect to the reference shape (that is a blob below the reference shape). <br>- Unchanged: Specifies an unchanged volume with respect to the reference (that is, a blob that overlaps the reference shape, and as such, indicates no change). |
| Sort Key | Specifies the logic by which the blobs of the referenced Blobs3D structure will be sorted. The available values are the following: <br>- None: No sorting logic will be applied to the list of blobs. Use this setting if you simply want a count of the blobs, or want to examine them without the need to order them. <br>- Volume: Sort the blobs by their volume. Use this setting if you want to examine the blobs sorted by their volume (e.g. from the largest volume to the smallest, or the opposite). This is the default setting. |

## ExtractCircle3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractCircle3D.htm`*

The ExtractCircle3D function extracts one ore more circles from the point cloud. It returns the extracted circles as a Circles3D structure, which can be referenced with Circle3D Vision Data Access functions. To use the ExtractCircle3D function:

- Insert the ExtractCircle3D function to the Spreadsheet:
- Drag and drop the function from the In-Sight Toolbox.
- Select a cell and use the Insert Function dialog.
- Select a cell and type the name of the function, followed by the "(" character. The Property Sheet pops up.
- Make sure that the PointCloud parameter refers to a cell that contains a point cloud. Adjust the default $A$0 value if needed.
- Double-click the Region3D parameter to open the interactive display, and adjust the ROI shape projected onto the acquisition display. Alternatively, you can expand the Region3D settings and define the parameters manually.
- Click OK to finalize the settings.

### Inputs

The ExtractCircle3D function has the following syntax: ExtractCircle3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Region3D,ExternalRegion,AcceptThreshold,NumberToExtract,DistanceThreshold,MinimumSharpness,MaximumSharpness,MaxAcceptableTilt,TransitionTypes,SortKey,SortOrder,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a Region3D defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Region3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Accept Threshold | Specifies the minimum score a result has to reach for the function to consider it a found circle. The value range is 0.000 to 100.000. The default setting is 50.000. |
| Number to Extract | Specifies the maximum number of circles the function extracts. The value range is 1 to inf. The default setting is 1. |
| Distance Threshold | Specifies the maximum distance in real-world units between an edgelet and a candidate circle for the edgelet to be considered an inlier of the candidate circle. Tip: Set the value of this parameter according to how noisy the point cloud is, and consider the order of the amplitude of the random fluctuations in the coordinate values. Depending on the type of vision system, the following value ranges are recommended by default: <br>- For In-Sight In-Sight L38 series vision systems, a value of 0.1 – 0.5 mm must suffice. If the point cloud's region of interest contains outlier Outliers are the subset of input points that fall outside a specified distance from a fitted geometric model, such as a sphere or cylinder. These points do not meet the user-defined distance threshold and are excluded from the model. A high number of outliers can indicate noise in the data or a poor model fit. points, such as spikes, then set this parameter lower than the typical height of the spikes. |
| Minimum Sharpness | Specifies the minimum acceptable sharpness of the circle, that is, the angular measurement between the support surfaces measured along the extraction direction. The value range is 0 to 30 degrees. |
| Maximum Sharpness | Specifies the maximum acceptable sharpness of the circle, that is, the angular measurement between the support surfaces measured along the extraction direction. The value range is 0 to 150 degrees. |
| Max Acceptable Tilt | Specifies the maximum angular deviation of the normal of the circle from the expected direction. The value range is 0 to 90 degrees, and the default value is 90. |
| Transition Types | Specifies whether to extract convex circles (0), concave circles (1), or both (2). By default, the function extracts both circle types. |
| Sort Key | Specifies the logic by which the extracted circles are sorted. The available values are the following: <br>- None: No sorting logic will be applied to the list of circles. Use this setting if you simply want a count of the circles, or want to examine them without the need to order them. <br>- Score: Sort the circles by their calculated score values. This is the default setting. <br>- Sharpness: Sort the circles by their sharpness. <br>- Radius: Sort the circles by their radius. <br>- Offset From Axis: Sort the circles by the amount they are offset from the axis. |
| Sort Order | Specifies whether to sort the results in ascending or descending order. Note: This parameter is disabled if Sort Key is set to None. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Circles3D structure containing the circles extracted from the point cloud, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

## ExtractClearSpot3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractClearSpot3D.htm`*

The ExtractClearSpot3D function allows you to extract one or more feature-free areas of a specified size, or clear spots, from the Region of Interest. This function is useful for cases such as finding an appropriate spot on a part for a label of a certain size, or calculating the maximum number of labels that can fit in a specific area. To use the ExtractClearSpot3D function:

- Drag and drop the ExtractClearSpot3D function into the Spreadsheet.
- In the Property Sheet that pops up, set up the Region of Interest using one of the following methods:
- Double-click the Box3D parameter and adjust the ROI box in the acquisition display.
- Expand the Box3D parameter and define the box parameters manually.
- Double-click the External Box parameter and select a Box3D function cell in Spreadsheet.
- Optionally, double-click the Exclude Region parameter and select a Region3D function cell in Spreadsheet to define an area that is excluded from the search region.
- Adjust the Spot parameters to define the size and position of the clear spots that you want the function to find.
- Adjust the Margin parameters to define the margins that you want the function to keep between the spots.
- Define the Results to Find paremeter to specify the number of clear spots you want the function to find.
- Adjust the Search Mode and Operation Mode parameters to fine-tune your results.

### Inputs

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Box3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the 3D rectangle of the function. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the box along the X-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeY The size of the box along the Y-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeZ The size of the box along the Z-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation of the box (in degrees) about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle of the box (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the tilt direction of the box (in degrees) from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Box is set to 0. |
| External Box3D | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Exclude Region | Specifies a reference to a Region3D structure defined in another cell. The function excludes the referenced Region3D structure from the Region of Interest for the function. |
| Spot | Specifies the size and position of the clear spots. The following Spot parameters are available: SizeX The size of the spot along the X-axis of the spot plane. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeY The size of the spot along the Y-axis of the spot plane. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. Minimum Point Coverage The minimum spot point coverage on the point cloud in percent (0 to 100). Maximum Overlap Ratio The maximum allowable overlap ratio between two neighboring spots in percent (0 to 100). Allow 90 Degree Rotation If enabled, the function can register clear spots that are rotated by 90 degrees on the XY plane. Maximum Spot Plane RMS The maximum allowable root mean square deviation of the clear spots on the observed plane. Maximum Spot Plane Tilt The maximum allowable plane tilt for the spot planes. Margin Specifies the margin between neighboring spots. The following Margin parameters are available: SizeX The size of the margin along the X-axis of the spot plane. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 5. SizeY The size of the margin along the Y-axis of the spot plane. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 5. Allow Margin Outside Workspace If enabled, the function can find spots using margins that are outside the defined Region of Interest. Minimum Point Coverage The minimum spot point coverage on the point cloud in percent (0 to 100). Height Tolerance Specifies the height tolerance for points outside the spot plane when calculating margins. Minimum Area in Tolerance Specifies the minimum spot margin area that must meet the height tolerance in percent (0 to 100). Search Mode Specifies the search mode. The following Search Mode parameters are available: |
| Search Mode | <br>- Highest (default): prioritize results with higher Z value relative to the bottom plane of the RoI. <br>- Closest to Preferred Location: prioritize results that are closest to the preferred location defined with the Preferred Location X and Preferred Location Y parameters. <br>- Highest and Closest to Preferred Location: prioritize results with a higher Z value relative to the bottom plane of the RoI, and closest to the preferred location defined with the Preferred Location X and Preferred Location Y parameters. <br>- Unspecified: results without specific criteria. |
| Height Tolerance | Specifies the height tolerance for high spots compared to the highest spot. Note: This parameter is only available when the Search Mode parameter is set to Highest and Closest to Preferred Location. |
| Preferred Location X | Specifies the relative X coordinate of the preferred location in the top plane of the RoI. Results with a center closest to this location are returned first when using the Closest to Preferred Location or Highest and Closest to Preferred Location search mode. |
| Preferred Location Y | Specifies the relative Y coordinate of the preferred location in the top plane of the RoI. Results with a center closest to this location are returned first when using the Closest to Preferred Location or Highest and Closest to Preferred Location search mode. |
| Results to Find Specifies the number of results to find. Operation Mode | Specifies the Operation Mode: <br>- Speed: this mode is recommended for cases where runtime is a critical consideration. <br>- Balanced (default): this mode is recommended for most cases. <br>- Accuracy: this mode is recommended for cases where the RoI does not represent a planar surface, and the Balanced mode is not returning acceptable results. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns
A ClearSpots3D data structure, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.
Results
Output
Description

The number of found spots.
Index
The index of each found spot.
Rectangle
A Rectangle3D structure around each found spot.

## ExtractCrossSection3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractCrossSection3D.htm`*

The ExtractCrossSection3D function allows you to extract a profile from a 3D point cloud by defining a rectangle in 3D space to use as a slicing object. The extracted profile uses the points where the slicing rectangle intersects with the 3D point cloud, flattening the points to two dimensions. The Region of Interest is effectively a 3D box based on the defined rectangle and the thickness parameter. The extracted profile allows you to perform height analysis, measurements, and other inspection tasks on a single cross-section of the acquired 3D point cloud using additional vision tools on the output Profile3D structure.

| 3D Point Cloud with ExtractCrossSection3D | Profile View |

The ExtractCrossSection3D function also allows you to use an External Fixture3D as input, which ensures that the function extracts the same profile for each acquisition. You can add a finding tool such as PatMax3D or Lines3D to create a fixture, and use the Fixture3D output of the finding tool as an External Fixture for the ExtractCrossSection3D function. Once the finding tool locates the trained feature for a new acquisition, the ExtractCrossSection3D function can use the located feature to align the Region of Interest in the 3D point cloud, and produce consistent profiles regardless of positioning inconsistencies in the acquisition. You can use the Profile3D output of the ExtractCrossSection3D function as input for profile feature extraction tools. Profile feature extraction tools allow you to extract Circle3D, Point3D, and Line3D structures from the profile.

### Inputs

The ExtractCrossSection3D function has the following syntax: ExtractCrossSection3D(PointCloud, Fixture3D, ExternalFixture, Rectangle3D, ExternalRectangle, Thickness, SampleDistance, GapFillSize, VerticalDiscontinuityMode, ZDiscontinuityThreshold, InsertCliffs, CliffLength, CliffXThreshold, Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Rectangle3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the 3D rectangle of the function. Double-click on the Rectangle3D parameter in the property sheet to adjust the rectangle on the acquisition display. Rectangle3D is offset from the PointCloud origin or the external fixture in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the rectangle along the PointCloud X-axis. SizeY The size of the rectangle along the PointCloud Y-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is only available if you set External Rectangle to 0. |
| External Rectangle | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell for constructing the 3D structure. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Rectangle3D structure of the function. |
| Thickness | Specifies the thickness of the slicing rectangle that the function uses to search for points. Thickness defines the size of the Region of Interest on the axis perpendicular to the profile. When you define a thickness greater than 0, the function picks up points that deviate from the slicing rectangle on the perpendicular axis by a distance up to half the defined thickness in both directions, creating a flattened composite profile from the registered points. |
| Sample Distance | Specifies the distance between sampling points for the profile creation. A small sample distance creates a profile that highlights surface imperfections and sudden peaks or valleys. A large sample distance creates a profile that can smooth over imperfections. |
| Gap Fill Size | Specifies the minimum distance on the Xp-axis of the extraction rectangle between adjacent points for identifying a gap in the profile. For adjacent points with a distance below the Gap Fill Size, the function creates a continuous profile. For adjacent points with a distance above the Gap Fill Size, the function displays a gap between the two points. |
| Vertical Discontinuity Mode | Specifies the method of compensating for discontinuity on the Zp-axis of the extraction rectangle between adjacent points: <br>- 0 = Interpolate: draws a direct line between the two points. <br>- 1 = Z Aligned: draws a vertical line aligned with the Zp-axis from the point with a larger Zp value. Z Discontinuity Threshold Specifies the maximum distance on the Zp-axis between adjacent points for which the function considers the profile to be continuous. Insert Cliffs Specifies whether the function inserts cliffs into the profile. The function inserts cliffs on either side of a gap, dropping the Zp-axis to a negative value. Inserting cliffs allows you to extract corner points from gaps. Cliff Length Specifies the length of the inserted cliffs. Cliff X Threshold Specifies the distance on the Xp-axis between adjacent points across a gap above which the function inserts cliffs. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Profile3D data structure containing the extracted profile, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

Num Found
Index
Profile

GetNFound(Profiles3D)

## ExtractCylinder3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractCylinder3D.htm`*

The ExtractCylinder3D function is used to extract multiple Cylinder3D structures from the point cloud. It returns the extracted 3D cylinders in a Cylinders3D structure.

### Inputs

The ExtractCylinder3D function has the following syntax: ExtractCylinder3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Region3D,ExternalRegion,NumberToExtract,DistanceThreshold,AcceptThreshold,ClutterPercentage,RadiusMin,RadiusMax,MaxAcceptableTilt,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Number to Extract | Specifies the maximum number of cylinders to extract. The value range is 1 to inf., and the default value is 1. |
| Distance Threshold | Specifies the distance (in real-world units) from the cylinder beyond which points are considered clutter. Tip: Set the value of this parameter according to how noisy the point cloud is, and consider the order of the amplitude of the random fluctuations in the coordinate values. Depending on the type of vision system, the following value ranges are recommended by default: <br>- For In-Sight In-Sight L38 series vision systems, a value of 0.1 – 0.5 mm must suffice. If the point cloud's region of interest contains outlier Outliers are the subset of input points that fall outside a specified distance from a fitted geometric model, such as a sphere or cylinder. These points do not meet the user-defined distance threshold and are excluded from the model. A high number of outliers can indicate noise in the data or a poor model fit. points, such as spikes, then set this parameter lower than the typical height of the spikes. Accept Threshold Specifies the minimum percentage score a result must have to be considered found by the function. The vale range is 0 – 100, and the default value is 50. Clutter Percentage Specifies the estimated percentage of clutter points, that is the points on edges that do not belong to any of the desired cylinders. The value range is 1 – 97, and the default value is 5). Tip: Lower values provide better performance, at the cost of robustness in the presence of clutter. Radius Min Specifies the lower bound on the value of the radius of the extracted cylinders. The value range is 0 to the value of the Maximum Radius attribute. The default value is 0. Radius Max Specifies the upper bound on the value of the radius of the extracted cylinders. The value range is from the value of the Minimum Radius attribute to inf., and the default value is 10000. Max. Acceptable Tilt Specifies the maximum angular deviation of the normal of the cylinder from the expected direction (in degrees). The value range is 0 to 90, and the default value is 90. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Cylinders3D data structure containing the 3D cylinders extracted from the point cloud, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

## ExtractDirectionHistogram3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractDirectionHistogram3D.htm`*

The ExtractDirectionHistogram3D function is used to extract a 3D direction histogram. It provides functions to compute the distribution of directions in a 3D space, between the surface normals on the point cloud and a reference plane. The function returns a Histogram3D structure.

### Inputs

The ExtractDirectionHistogram3D function has the following syntax: ExtractDirectionHistogram3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Region3D,ExternalRegion,Plane3D,ExternalPlane,FixtureReference,BinSize,FeatureSize,MinTiltAngle,MaxTiltAngle,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Max. Tilt Angle | Specifies the maximum tilt angle. The value range is from the configured value of the Min. Tilt Angle parameter to 90, and the default value is 90. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The region of interest and the reference plane will be displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. Note: You can use Plane3D to mask data for training. The Plane3D function prevents the tool from taking any points that belong to that plane and are within the ROI. |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. |
| Fixture Reference | Specifies whether to fixture the reference plane. Consider the following when using this setting: <br>- If you define the reference plane relative to a point cloud part, it will be fixtured using the same fixture as the tool's Region of Interest. <br>- If the Plane3D structure used for the function is extracted with an Extract function (such as ExtractPlane3D), then the plane is already fixtured, and this parameter can be disabled. This parameter is enabled by default. |
| Bin Size | Specifies the size of the intervals in which the values are grouped. The value range is 1 to 180., and the default value is 1. |
| Feature Size | Specifies the sampling quality of point cloud points and patches used for computing surface normals. The quality has three levels: <br>- 0 = Large <br>- 1 = Medium (Default) <br>- 2 = Small Tip: <br>- Lower values (Large and Medium) increase vision tool performance, but result in less accurate normal estimations and noise data sensitivity. <br>- The Small value results in more accurate normal estimations and better noise data sensitivity, at the cost of performance. |
| Min. Tilt Angle | Specifies the minimum tilt angle. The value range is 0 to the configured value of the Max. Tilt Angle parameter, and the default value is 0. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 3 = input and chart | The region of interest, the reference plane and the histogram chart will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Histogram3D data structure containing the direction histogram extracted from the point cloud, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

### Vision Data Access functions

The following Histogram3D Vision Data Access functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create the result table:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| GetSumOfFrequencies(Histogram3D, [Low], [High]) | Returns the number of 3D points within the specified threshold range. <br>- In the Low Count column, it returns the number of 3D points below the threshold (returned by the GetThreshold function). <br>- In the High Count column, it returns the number of 3D points above the threshold (returned by the GetThreshold function). |
| GetThreshold(Histogram3D) | Computes an optimum histogram threshold that does a binary segmentation of all the histogram data. That way, GetThreshold specifies a threshold level that maximizes similarity between the histogram function's 3D region of interest and all possible binary re-quantization. |
| GetMean(Histogram3D) | Returns the mean value of the 3D points by summing up the values for all points in the function's 3D region of interest and then dividing by the count of 3D points in the same range. |
| GetStandardDeviation(Histogram3D) | Returns the standard deviation of the 3D points within the function's 3D region of interest. |

The ExtractDistanceHistogram3D function is used to extract a 3D distance histogram. It provides functions to compute the distribution of distances from the points in a point cloud to:

- A specific point in space.
- A specific line.

The function returns a Histogram3D structure.

### Inputs

The ExtractDistanceHistogram3D function has the following syntax: ExtractDistanceHistogram3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture, Region3D,ExternalRegion,Mode,Point3D,ExternalPoint,Plane3D,ExternalPlane,Line3D,ExternalLine,FixtureReference,BinSize,MinValue,MaxValue,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Max. Value | Specifies the maximum value of distances to compute in the histogram. The value range is from the configured value of the Min. Value parameter to inf., and the default value is 10000. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The region of interest and the reference plane will be displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Mode | Specifies the mode of operation: <br>- 0 = Center of Mass: Calculates the center of mass of all points in the ROI. Then, it fills the histogram with absolute distances from the center of mass to each point in the point cloud. This is the default setting. <br>- 1 = Point: Fills the histogram with absolute distances from a specific point, provided by a caller to each point in the point cloud. <br>- 2 = Plane: Fills the histogram with signed distances from a specific plane, provided by a caller to each point in the point cloud. |
| - | 3 = Line: Fills the histogram with absolute distances from a specific line, provided by a caller to each point in the point cloud. |
| Point3D | Specifies the offset of the 3D point to use. It is offset from the PointCloud (or Fixture3D, if Fixture Reference is enabled) origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Point is set to 0. Note: This parameter is only available if the Mode is set to Point, and External Point is not 0. |

External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. Note: You can use Plane3D to mask data for training. The Plane3D function prevents the tool from taking any points that belong to that plane and are within the ROI. | External Line | Specifies a reference to the Line3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Line3D structure instead. Note: This parameter is only available if the Mode is set to Line. |

Consider the following when using this setting: <br>- If you define the reference plane relative to a point cloud part, it will be fixtured using the same fixture as the tool's Region of Interest. <br>- If the Plane3D structure used for the function is extracted with an Extract function (such as ExtractPlane3D), then the plane is already fixtured, and this parameter can be disabled. This parameter is enabled by default. Note: This parameter is only available if the Mode parameter is set to Point or Plane. |
| Bin Size | Specifies the size of the intervals in which the values are grouped. |
| Min. Value | Specifies the minimum value of distances to compute in the histogram. The value range is -inf. to the configured value of the Max. Value parameter, and the default value is -10000. |

## ExtractEdge3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractEdge3D.htm`*

The ExtractEdge3D function is used to extract edges as Line3D structures from the specified region of the point cloud. The edges start at one plane of the specified 3D box Region of Interest (ROI), and extend to the opposite plane of the box. Each extracted edge is roughly parallel to a specific edge of the box, called the canonical edge. The extracted edges are classified as either convex or concave, depending on the surface characteristics along the extraction direction. The extracted edges are returned in an Edges3D structure.

| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Surface Length | Specifies the length of the support surfaces perpendicular to the expected edge. Accept Threshold Specifies the minimum acceptance percentage threshold of the edges. The value range is 1 to 100, and the default value is 50. Minimum Coverage Specifies the minimum coverage amount. Coverage is the percentage of the support surfaces where the edge exists. Missing data on the edge will reduce coverage. |
| Number to Extract | Specifies the number of edges to extract in the ROI. The value range is 1 to inf., and the default value is 1. |
| Transition Types | Specifies whether to extract convex edges (0), concave edges (1), or both (2). By default, both edge types are extracted. Minimum Sharpness Specifies the minimum acceptable sharpness of the edges (in degrees). The value range is 0 to the configured value of the Maximum Sharpness attribute, and the default value is 30. Maximum Sharpness Specifies the maximum acceptable sharpness of the edges (in degrees). The value range is from the configured value of the Minimum Sharpness attribute to 180, and the default value is 150. Maximum Vertical Angle Specifies the maximum acceptable vertical angle of the edges (in degrees). The vertical angle is measured between the canonical edge and the projection of the extraction edge onto the bottom plane of the ROI. The value range is 0 to 45, and the default value is 45. Maximum Horizontal Angle Specifies the maximum acceptable horizontal angle of the edges (in degrees). The horizontal angle is measured between the canonical edge and the projection of the extraction edge onto the bottom plane of the ROI. The value range is 0 to 45, and the default value is 45. Surface Separation Specifies the separation between support surfaces. The value range is 0 to inf., and the default value is 0. Tip: Use this parameter to detect rounded or beveled edges |
| Feature Size | Specifies the sampling quality of the point cloud points and patches that will be used for edge extraction. The available values are the following: <br>- 0 = Large: Calculate extraction using large features. <br>- 1 = Medium: Calculate extraction using medium features. <br>- 2 = Small: Calculate extraction using small features. This is the default setting. Tip: <br>- Lower values (Large and Medium) increase extraction performance, but are less accurate. <br>- The Small value results in more accurate extraction and better noise data sensitivity, at the cost of performance. |
| Sort Key | Specifies the logic by which the extracted edges will be sorted. The available values are the following: <br>- None: No sorting logic will be applied to the list of edges. Use this setting if you simply want a count of the edges, or want to examine them without the need to order them. <br>- Score: The extract edges are sorted by their score value. <br>- Coverage: The extracted edges are sorted by their coverage. <br>- Sharpness: The extracted edges are sorted by their sharpness. <br>- Vertical Angle: The extracted edges are sorted by their vertical angles. <br>- Horizontal Angle: The extracted edges are sorted by their horizontal angles. <br>- Position Along Extraction Direction: The extracted edges are sorted by their positions along the extraction direction. This is the default setting. <br>- Transition Type: The extracted edges are sorted by their transition types. Note: When this key is selected, Ascending sort order means that convex edges are listed before concave edges. When Descending sort order is selected, concave edges are listed before convex edges. <br>- Edge Segment Center Spoke Angle: The extracted edges are sorted by the spoke angle of the edge segment's center. <br>- Edge Segment Center Spoke Radius: The extracted edges are sorted by the spoke radius of the edge segment's center. |
| Sort Order | Specifies whether to sort the results in ascending or descending order. Note: This parameter is disabled if Sort Key is set to None. |
| Sort Reference | Specifies the origin of the coordinate space in which the positional and rotational values are defined. The available values are the following: <br>- Camera: The coordinate space is based off the system in which the point cloud's points are defined. <br>- Region: The coordinate space is based off the coordinate system of the working region used in the job. Note: This parameter is enabled only if External Region is set to 0, and Sort Key is set to Coverage, Edge Segment Center Spoke Angle, or Edge Segment Center Spoke Radius. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

An Edges3D data structure containing the edges extracted from the point cloud, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

## ExtractParallelCrossSections3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractParallelCrossSections3D.htm`*

The ExtractParallelCrossSections3D function allows you to extract multiple parallel profiles from a 3D point cloud by defining a 3D Region of Interest and the distance between the extracted profiles. The function creates parallel planes within the Region of Interest, offset from each other by the defined step distance. Each plane serves as a slicing object, creating a profile using the points where the plane intersects with the 3D point cloud. The planes for each profile are parallel to the X and Z axes of the Region of Interest.

| 3D Point Cloud with ExtractParallelCrossSections3D | Profile View of Profile3D 1 |

The ExtractParallelCrossSections3D function also allows you to use an External Fixture3D as input, which ensures that the function extracts the same profile for each acquisition. You can add a finding tool such as PatMax3D or Lines3D to create a fixture, and use the Fixture3D output of the finding tool as an External Fixture for the ExtractParallelCrossSections3D function. Once the finding tool locates the trained feature for a new acquisition, the ExtractParallelCrossSections3D function can use the located feature to align the Region of Interest in the 3D point cloud, and produce consistent profiles regardless of positioning inconsistencies in the acquisition. You can use the Profile3D outputs of the ExtractParallelCrossSections3D function as input for profile feature extraction tools. Profile feature extraction tools allow you to extract Circle3D, Point3D, and Line3D structures from the profile.

### Inputs

The ExtractParallelCrossSections3D function has the following syntax: ExtractParallelCrossSections3D(PointCloud, Fixture3D, ExternalFixture, Region3D, ExternalRegion, StepDistance, StepOffset, Thickness, SampleDistance, GapFillSize, VerticalDiscontinuityMode, ZDiscontinuityThreshold, InsertCliffs, CliffLength, CliffXThreshold, Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. Step Distance Specifies the distance between adjacent slicing rectangles within the Region of Interest. The number of slicing rectangles depends on the number of steps that the tool can complete within the Region of Interest. Step Offset Specifies the distance of the first slicing rectangle on the Y-axis from the origin of the Region of Interest. Thickness Specifies the thickness of the slicing rectangle that the function uses to search for points. When you define a thickness greater than 0, the function picks up points that deviate from the slicing rectangle on the perpendicular axis by a distance up to half the defined thickness in both directions, creating a flattened composite profile from the registered points. |
| Sample Distance | Specifies the distance between sampling points for the profile creation. A small sample distance creates a profile that highlights surface imperfections and sudden peaks or valleys. A large sample distance creates a profile that can smooth over imperfections. |
| Gap Fill Size | Specifies the minimum distance on the Xp-axis of the extraction rectangle between adjacent points for identifying a gap in the profile. For adjacent points with an Xp-axis distance below the Gap Fill Size, the function creates a continuous profile. For adjacent points with an Xp-axis distance above the Gap Fill Size, the function displays a gap between the two points. |
| Vertical Discontinuity Mode | Specifies the method of compensating for discontinuity on the Zp-axis of the extraction rectangle between adjacent points: <br>- 0 = Interpolate: draws a direct line between the two points. <br>- 1 = Z Aligned: draws a vertical line aligned with the Zp-axis from the point with a larger Zp value. |
| Z Discontinuity Threshold | Specifies the minimum distance on the Zp-axis between adjacent points for which the function considers the profile to be discontinuous. For adjacent points with a Zp-axis distance below the Z Discontinuity Threshold, the function creates a continuous profile. For adjacent points with a Zp-axis distance above the Z Discontinuity Threshold, the function creates a gap between the two points. |
| Insert Cliffs | Specifies whether the function inserts cliffs into the profile. The function inserts cliffs on either side of a gap, dropping the Zp-axis to a negative value. Inserting cliffs allows you to extract corner points from gaps. Cliff Length Specifies the length of the inserted cliffs. Cliff X Threshold Specifies the distance on the Xp-axis between adjacent points across a gap above which the function inserts cliffs. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |
