## ExtractPlane3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractPlane3D.htm`*

The ExtractPlane3D function is used to extract one or more planes from a point cloud in a user defined region of interest (ROI). The orientation of the extracted planes is determined by the ROI. The tool has two modes for plane extraction:

- Fast mode, using all points to do a least squares fit. This mode extracts a single plane by Orthogonal Distance Regression.
- Robust mode, using random sample consensus (RANSAC).

The extracted planes are returned in an Planes3D structure.

### Inputs

The ExtractHeight3D function has the following syntax: ExtractPlane3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Region3D,ExternalRegion,Mode,NumberToExtract,DistanceThreshold,ClutterPercentage,MaxAcceptableTilt,SortKey,SortOrder,SortReference,ResultGraphic,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Mode | Specifies the extraction mode: <br>- 0 = Fast mode. In this mode, the function extracts a single plane using all points (including clutter) within the region of interest. If the scene in the function's ROI contains more than one plane, a single compromise plane is fit to the points of the point cloud. This is the function's fastest mode of operation, but it is vulnerable to the presence of outliers in the region. <br>- 1 = Robust mode. In this mode, the function can extract multiple planes even in the midst of clutter, and can reject noise and clutter by configuring the Distance Threshold and Clutter Percentage parameters. The Distance Threshold parameter is used to define clutter points, while Clutter Percentage is used to define the amount of clutter within the region of interest. This is the default setting, and is recommended to use if you either want to extract multiple planes, or you need to work with a point cloud acquisition with outlier Outliers are the subset of input points that fall outside a specified distance from a fitted geometric model, such as a sphere or cylinder. These points do not meet the user-defined distance threshold and are excluded from the model. A high number of outliers can indicate noise in the data or a poor model fit. points in the region. |
| Number to Extract | Specifies the number of planes to extract. The value range is 1 to inf., and the default value is 1. Note: This setting is restricted to 1 when Fast mode is set, and the function is not in an erroneous state. |
| Distance Threshold | Specifies the distance from the plane beyond which the points are considered clutter. The value range is 0 to inf., and the default value is 1. Note: This setting is only available in Robust mode, and when the function is not in an erroneous state. Tip: Set the value of this parameter according to how noisy the point cloud is, and consider the order of the amplitude of the random fluctuations in the coordinate values. Depending on the type of vision system, the following value ranges are recommended by default: <br>- For In-Sight In-Sight L38 series vision systems, a value of 0.1 – 0.5 mm must suffice. If the point cloud's region of interest contains outlier points, such as spikes, then set this parameter lower than the typical height of the spikes. |
| Clutter Percentage | Specifies the estimated percentage of clutter points, that is the points that do not belong to any of the desired planes. The value range is 1 to 95 and the default value is 5. Note: This setting is only available in Robust mode, and when the function is not in an erroneous state. Tip: Lower values provide faster performance at the cost of robustness in the presence of clutter. Max. Acceptable Tilt Specifies the maximum angular deviation of the normal of the plane from the expected direction. The value range is 0 to 90 and the default value is 90. Sort Key Specifies the sorting logic for the planes in the Planes3D structure. The available values are the following: <br>- None: No sorting logic will be applied. Use this setting if you simply want to count the sorted planes, or want to examine them without the need to order them. <br>- Score: Sort the planes by their calculated score values. <br>- Number of Inliers: Sort the planes by their number of inliers. <br>- Residuals RMS: Sort the planes by the root mean square of their residuals. <br>- Residuals Max: Sort the planes by their maximum residuals. <br>- Inlier Density Over Rectangle: Sort the planes by the density of their inliers over their rectangles. <br>- Area of Rectangle: Sort the planes by the area of their finite rectangles. <br>- Relative Pitch: Sort the planes by their relative pitches. <br>- Center of Rectangle X: Sort the planes by the X-axis distance of their rectangle's center point from the origin of the point cloud space. <br>- Center of Rectangle Y: Sort the planes by the Y-axis distance of their rectangle's center point from the origin of the point cloud space. <br>- Center of Rectangle Z: Sort the planes by the Z-axis distance of their rectangle's center point from the origin of the point cloud space. <br>- Center of Rectangle R: Sort the planes by the radial distance of their rectangle's center point from the origin of the point cloud space. <br>- Center of Rectangle Spoke Angle: Sort the planes by their angle from their rectangle's center's X-axis and Y-axis position to their origin. <br>- Center of Rectangle Spoke Radius: Sort the planes by the center of their rectangle's distance from their origin to the center of their patch's location on the X-axis and Y-axis (disregarding the Z-axis height). |
| Sort Order | Specifies whether to sort the planes of the referenced Planes3D structure in ascending or descending order. Note: This parameter is not available if the Sort Key parameter is set to None. |
| Sort Reference | Specifies the origin of the coordinate space in which the positional and rotational values are defined. The available values are the following: <br>- Camera: The coordinate space is based off the system in which the point cloud's points are defined. <br>- Region: The coordinate space is based off the coordinate system of the working region used in the job. Note: This parameter is enabled only if External Region is set to 0, and Sort Key is set to any of the Center of Rectangle values. |
| Result Graphic | Selects the type of graphics to use for showing the results: <br>- 0 = Surface (default) <br>- 1 = Plane |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Planes3D data structure extracted from the point cloud, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. | Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. Note: You can use Plane3D to mask data for training. The Plane3D function prevents the tool from taking any points that belong to that plane and are within the ROI. Note: This parameter works only if the Reference Plane setting is set to Plane, and External Plane is not 0 |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. Note: This parameter works only if the Reference Plane setting is set to Plane. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

## ExtractPolylineCrossSections3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractPolylineCrossSections3D.htm`*

The ExtractPolylineCrossSections3D function allows you to extract multiple profiles from a 3D point cloud using a 2D polyline path created with the EditPolylinePath function. The function extracts profiles perpendicular to the 2D polyline at a defined distance interval.

| Polyline input | Output cross sections |

### Inputs

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Profile Continuity | Gap Fill Size |
| Cliff Parameters | Insert Cliffs |
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. External 2D Polyline Path Specifies a reference to an EditPolylinePath structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell to generate perpendicular profiles along the polyline. Mode Specifies the mode used by the function to create the profiles: <br>- Single Background Plane <br>- Multiple Background Planes <br>- Vertices Atop Surface Step Distance Specifies the distance between the perpendicular profiles generated by the function. The number of profiles generated depends on the number of steps that the tool can complete along the polyline. Step Offset Specifies the offset of the first profile from the start of the polyline. Cross Section Size X Specifies the size of the generated profiles along the X-axis. Cross Section Size Z Specifies the size of the generated profiles along the Z-axis. Nominal Z's Tilt Specifies the tilt of the nominal Z-axis for the generated profiles in degrees (0 – 180). Nominal Z's Tilt Direction Specifies the tilt direction of the nominal Z-axis for the generated profiles in degrees (0 – 360). Thickness Specifies the neighborhood range of the slicing planes used to generate profiles. When you define a thickness greater than 0, the function picks up points that deviate from the slicing planes on the perpendicular axis by a distance up to half the defined thickness in both directions, creating a flattened composite profile from the registered points. |
| Sample Distance | Specifies the sampling distance within the slicing planes used to generate profiles. A small sample distance creates a profile that highlights surface imperfections and sudden peaks or valleys. A large sample distance creates a profile that can smooth over imperfections. |
|  | Specifies the minimum distance on the X-axis of the slicing plane between adjacent points for identifying a gap in the profile. For adjacent points with an X-axis distance below the Gap Fill Size, the function creates a continuous profile. For adjacent points with an X-axis distance above the Gap Fill Size, the function displays a gap between the two points. |
| Vertical Discontinuity Mode | Specifies the method of compensating for discontinuity on the Z-axis of the slicing plane between adjacent points: <br>- 0 = Interpolate: draws a direct line between the two points. <br>- 1 = Z Aligned: draws a vertical line aligned with the Z-axis from the point with a larger Z value. |
| Z Discontinuity Threshold | Specifies the minimum distance on the Z-axis between adjacent points for which the function considers the profiles to be discontinuous. For adjacent points with a Z-axis distance below the Z Discontinuity Threshold, the function creates a continuous profile. For adjacent points with a Z-axis distance above the Z Discontinuity Threshold, the function creates a gap between the two points. |
|  | Specifies whether the function inserts cliffs into the profiles. The function inserts cliffs on either side of a gap, dropping the Z-axis to a negative value. Inserting cliffs allows you to extract corner points from gaps. Cliff Length Specifies the length of the inserted cliffs. Cliff X Threshold Specifies the distance on the X-axis between adjacent points across a gap above which the function inserts cliffs. Show Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

## ExtractRadialCrossSections3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractRadialCrossSections3D.htm`*

The ExtractRadialCrossSections3D function allows you to extract profiles from a 3D point cloud by defining planes to use as slicing objects. The extracted profiles use the points where the Region of Interest intersects with the 3D point cloud, flattening the points to two dimensions. The tool creates multiple radial cross sections along the Region3D based on the Step Distance parameter. The extracted profiles allow you to perform height analysis, measurements, and other inspection tasks on cross-sections of the acquired 3D point cloud using additional vision tools on the output Profile3D structure. The ExtractRadialCrossSections3D function also allows you to use an External Region3D as input, which ensures that the function extracts the same profile for each acquisition. You can add a finding tool such as PatMax3D or Lines3D to create a fixture, and use the Fixture3D output of the finding tool as an External Fixture for the ExtractRadialCrossSections3D function. Once the finding tool locates the trained feature for a new acquisition, the ExtractRadialCrossSections3D function can use the located feature to align the Region of Interest in the 3D point cloud, and produce consistent profiles regardless of positioning inconsistencies in the acquisition. You can use the Profile3D output of the ExtractRadialCrossSectiosn3D function as input for profile feature extraction tools. Profile feature extraction tools allow you to extract Circle3D, Point3D, and Line3D structures from the profiles. To use the ExtractRadialCrossSections3D function:

- Drag and drop the ExtractRadialCrossSections3D function into the Spreadsheet.
- In the property sheet that pops up, either define the Region3D parameter manually or double-click the parameter to select a cell containing the Region structure you want the function to use.
- Define the Step Distance between the adjacent slicing planes.
- Define the Step Offset distance of the first slicing plane from the origin of the box in the Y direction.
- Click OK to finalize the settings.

### Inputs

The ExtractRadialCrossSections3D function has the following syntax: ExtractRadialCrossSections3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,ExternalRegion3D,StepDistance,StepOffset,Thickness,SampleDistance,ProfileContinuity,CliffParameters,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Profile Continuity | Gap Fill Size |
| Cliff Parameters | Insert Cliffs |
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |

SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. Curve The angle between the sides. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. ## ExtractSphere3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ExtractSphere3D.htm`*

The ExtractSphere3D function is used to extract one or more spheres from a point cloud in a user defined region of interest (ROI). The tool has two modes for sphere extraction:

- Fast mode, using all points to do a least squares fit. This mode extracts a single sphere by fitting the coefficients of a quadratic equation.
- Robust mode, using random sample consensus (RANSAC).

If no sphere is found by the function with the provided configuration, it returns a result with zero length shape, inliers, and residuals. Typically, radius range, math singularity or shape degeneracy can lead to not finding spheres. For example, if all input points are coincident, then the function cannot extract spheres. The function returns an Spheres3D structure.

### Inputs

The ExtractSphere3D function has the following syntax: ExtractSphere3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalRegion,Region3D,ExternalRegion,Mode,NumberToExtract,DistanceThreshold,AcceptThreshold,ClutterPercentage,RadiusMin,RadiusMax,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Mode | Specifies the extraction mode: <br>- 0 = Fast mode. In this mode, the function extracts a single sphere using all points (including clutter) within the region of interest. If the scene in the function's ROI contains more than one sphere, a single compromise sphere is extracted. This is the function's fastest mode of operation, but it is vulnerable to the presence of outliers in the region. <br>- 1 = Robust mode. In this mode, the function can extract multiple spheres even in the midst of clutter, and can reject noise and clutter by configuring the Distance Threshold and Clutter Percentage parameters. The Distance Threshold parameter is used to define clutter points, while Clutter Percentage is used to define the amount of clutter within the region of interest. This is the default setting, and is recommended to use if you either want to extract multiple spheres, or you need to work with a point cloud acquisition with outlier Outliers are the subset of input points that fall outside a specified distance from a fitted geometric model, such as a sphere or cylinder. These points do not meet the user-defined distance threshold and are excluded from the model. A high number of outliers can indicate noise in the data or a poor model fit. points in the region. |
| Number to Extract | Specifies the number of spheres to extract. The value range is 1 to inf., and the default value is 1. Note: This setting is restricted to 1 when Fast mode is set. |
| Distance Threshold | Specifies the distance from the sphere beyond which the points are considered clutter. The value range is 0 to inf., and the default value is 1. Note: This setting is only available in Robust mode. Tip: Set the value of this parameter according to how noisy the point cloud is, and consider the order of the amplitude of the random fluctuations in the coordinate values. Depending on the type of vision system, the following value ranges are recommended by default: <br>- For In-Sight In-Sight L38 series vision systems, a value of 0.1 – 0.5 mm must suffice. If the point cloud's region of interest contains outlier points, such as spikes, then set this parameter lower than the typical height of the spikes. Accept Threshold Specifies the minimum acceptance score of the results. The value range is 1 to 100, and the default value is 50. Clutter Percentage Specifies the estimated percentage of clutter points, that is the points that do not belong to any of the desired spheres. The value range is 1 to 95 and the default value is 5. Note: This setting is only available in Robust mode. Tip: Lower values provide faster performance at the cost of robustness in the presence of clutter. Radius Min Specifies the lower bound on the radius of the extracted spheres. The value range is 0 to the value of the Radius Max property, and the default value is 0. Radius Max Specifies the upper bound on the radius of the extracted spheres. The value range is from the value of the Radius Min attribute to inf., and the default value is 1000. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

Returns

A Spheres3D data structure extracted from the point cloud, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Exclude Base Plane | When enabled, the function adds a separate planar region of interest (ROI), so that the surface plane can be excluded when training or finding a 3D pattern, improving the performance of the tool. This setting is disabled by default, as undesired areas can also be excluded with appropriate placement of the Box3D structure. |
| Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. Note: You can use Plane3D to mask data for training. The Plane3D function prevents the tool from taking any points that belong to that plane and are within the ROI. Note: This parameter is available only if Exclude Base Plane is True and External Plane is 0. |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. Note: This parameter is available only if Exclude Base Plane is True. Offset Specifies the signed distance to the offset base plane. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 1. Model3D Specifies a reference to a trained Model3D structure trained with the TrainPatMax3D function in another cell. Num to Find Specifies the number of pattern instances to find. The value range is 1 to inf., and the default value is 1. Accept Threshold Specifies the minimum percentage score that a result must have to be considered a found pattern. The value range is 0 to 100, and the default value is 50. Max In-Plane Rotation Angle Specifies the maximum in-plane rotation angle that a result can have to be considered a found pattern. The value range is 0 to 180 and the default value is 180. |
| Max Tilt Angle | Specifies the maximum tilt rotation angle that a result can have to be considered a found pattern. The value range is 0 to 180 and the default value is 90. |
| Sort Key | Specifies the logic by which the found objects are sorted. The available values are the following: <br>- None: No sorting logic will be applied. Use this setting if you simply want a count of the objects, or want to examine them without the need to order them. <br>- Score: Sort the objects by their score. This is the default setting. <br>- Pose Rotation In-Plane Rotation Angle Norm: Sort the objects by their pose rotation's norm in-plane rotation. <br>- Pose Rotation In-Plane Rotation Angle Abs: Sort the objects by their pose rotation's absolute in-plane rotation. <br>- Pose Rotation Tilt Direction Norm: Sort the objects by their pose rotation's norm tilt direction. <br>- Pose Rotation Tilt Direction Abs: Sort the objects by their pose rotation's absolute tilt direction. <br>- Pose Rotation Tilt Angle: Sort the objects by their pose rotation's tilt angle. <br>- Pose Translation X: Sort the objects by their pose translation's X-component. <br>- Pose Translation Y: Sort the objects by their pose translation's Y-component. <br>- Pose Translation Z: Sort the objects by their pose translation's Z-component. <br>- Pose Translation R: Sort the objects by their pose translation's Euclidean distance. <br>- Pose Translation Spoke Angle Norm: Sort the objects by their pose translation's normalized spoke angle. <br>- Pose Translation Spoke Angle Abs: Sort the objects by their pose translation's absolute spoke angle. <br>- Pose Translation Spoke Radius: Sort the objects by their pose translation's spoke radius. <br>- Pose Translation X then Y then Z: Sort the objects by their pose translation's Grid X then Y, and then Z. <br>- Pose Translation Y then X then Z: Sort the objects by their pose translation's Grid Y then X, and then Z. |
| Sort Order | Specifies whether to sort the results in ascending or descending order. Note: This parameter is disabled if Sort Key is set to None. |
| Sort Tolerance | Specifies a threshold to determine if 2 or more results are tied. If they are tied, they can be sorted by a subsequent sort. Only takes effect when multiple sorting rules are applied (such as grid sorting or appending a sort tool). Note: This parameter is disabled if Sort Key is set to None. |
| Sort Reference | Specifies the origin of the coordinate space in which the positional and rotational values are defined. The available values are the following: <br>- Camera: The coordinate space is based off the system in which the point cloud's points are defined. <br>- Region: The coordinate space is based off the coordinate system of the working region used in the job. Note: This parameter is disabled if: <br>- The Sort Key is set to None or Score. <br>- An External Region is configured. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |
|  | Controls the color coding of the deviation heatmap on the 3D visualizer. The visualizer only displays the deviation heatmap while the FindPatMax3D property sheet is open. The deviation heatmap allows you to check the part alignment and deviations from the trained model while you are configuring the FindPatMax3D tool. Note: The deviation heatmap is only available if the TrainPatMax3D function was trained with In-Sight Vision Suite version 26.1 or later. To display deviation for jobs created in earlier versions, re-train the TrainPatMax3D function with a newer version. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Patterns3D data structure containing the found patterns, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

- **Num Found**：Index
- **Score**：Fixture
- **X**：Y
- **Z**：Rotation

## Fixture3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/Fixture3D.htm`*

The Fixture3D function allows you to set up fixturing coordinates that can be used by other 3D Vision Tools. It returns a Fixture3D structure containing the configured fixture coordinates.

### Inputs

The Fixture3D function has the following syntax: Fixture3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Fixture3D structure containing the parameters of the configured fixture coordinates, or #ERR if any parameter has been configured incorrectly.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the following functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create a result table.

- **X**：Y
- **Z**：Rotation
- **Tilt**：TiltDirection

| ❒Fixture3D

| GetX(Fixture3D) | GetY(Fixture3D) |
| GetZ(Fixture3D) | GetRotation(Fixture3D) |
| GetTilt(Fixture3D) | GetTiltDirection(Fixture3D) |

### Vision Data Access functions

The following Structures 3D Vision Data Access functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create the result table:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
|  | GetRotation(Fixture3D) Returns the rotation of the Z-axis in degrees, also known as the in-plane rotation. GetTilt(Fixture3D) Returns the tilt angle of the Fixture3D structure in degrees on the Z-axis. GetTiltDirection(Fixture3D) Returns the tilt direction angle of the specified Fixture3D structure in degrees. The angle is measured in the X-Y plane of the original reference coordinate system, and specifies the direction for the projection of the tilted Z-axis onto that plane. GetX(Fixture3D) Returns the X-axis coordinate of the fixture's center point. GetY(Fixture3D) Returns the Y-axis coordinate of the fixture's center point. GetZ(Fixture3D) Returns the Z-axis coordinate of the fixture's center point. |

## FixtureFromLines3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/FixtureFromLines3D.htm`*

The FixtureFromLines3D function is used to construct a fixture from two Line3D structures. The resulting fixture is returned as a Fixture3D structure.

- **3D Fixture Axis Color**：3D Fixture Axis
- **Red**：X
- **Green**：Y
- **Blue**：Z

To create a 3D fixture using the FixtureFromLines3D function, define two Line3D structures for the function to use. The function defines the 3D fixture based on the input structures in the following way:

- The origin of the output 3D fixture is the intersection point between the two input lines, or if they are not on the same plane and do not intersect, the mid-point of the shortest perpendicular line between the two input lines.
- The X-axis of the output 3D fixture is aligned with the first input line, with the positive direction of the X-axis aligned with the positive direction of the input line. The direction of the input line is from the first point to the second point of the input line.
- The Z-axis of the output 3D fixture is perpendicular to both input lines, with a positive direction determined by the right-hand rule from the first line to the second line. Note: The function creates the 3D fixture so that the positive direction of the fixture Z-axis always corresponds with the positive direction of the point cloud coordinate Z-axis. If the general rule would create a fixture Z-axis with a positive direction that aligns with the negative direction of the point cloud coordinate Z-axis, the function inverts the fixture Z-axis, and consequently the Y-axis.
- The Y-axis of the output 3D fixture is perpendicular to the X and Z axes, with a positive direction determined by the right-hand rule from the Z-axis to the X-axis.

### Inputs

The FixtureFromLines3D function has the following syntax: FixtureFromLines3D(PointCloud,Line3D0,ExternalLine0,Line3D1,ExternalLine1,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Line3D 0 | Specifies the offsets of the first 3D line to use for fixturing. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1} X0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. X1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. External Line 0 Specifies a reference to a Line3D structure defined in another cell to be used for fixturing. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Line3D structure instead for the first line. |
| Line3D 1 | Specifies the offsets of the second 3D line to use for fixturing. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1} X0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. X1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. External Line 1 Specifies a reference to a Line3D structure defined in another cell to be used for fixturing. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Line3D structure instead for the second line. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Fixture3D structure that stores 3D fixture coordinates.

## FixtureFromPointAndLine3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/FixtureFromPointAndLine3D.htm`*

The FixtureFromPointAndLine3D function is used to construct a fixture from a Point3D structure and a Line3D structure. The resulting fixture is returned as a Fixture3D structure.

- **3D Fixture Axis Color**：3D Fixture Axis
- **Red**：X
- **Green**：Y
- **Blue**：Z

To create a 3D fixture using the FixtureFromPointandLine3D function, define a Point3D structure and a Line3D structure for the function to use. The function defines the 3D fixture based on the input structures in the following way:

- The origin of the output 3D fixture is the projection point of the input point on the input line.
- The X-axis of the output 3D fixture is aligned with the input line, with the positive direction of the X-axis aligned with the positive direction of the input line.
- The Y-axis of the output 3D fixture is aligned with the line that runs through the origin and the input point, with a positive direction toward the input point.
- The Z-axis of the output 3D fixture is perpendicular to the X and Y axes, with a positive direction defined by the right-hand rule from the X-axis to the Y-axis. Note: The function creates the 3D fixture so that the positive direction of the fixture Z-axis always corresponds with the positive direction of the point cloud coordinate Z-axis. If the general rule would create a fixture Z-axis with a positive direction that aligns with the negative direction of the point cloud coordinate Z-axis, the function inverts the fixture Z-axis, and consequently the Y-axis.

| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |

## FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D.htm`*

The FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D function constructs a fixture that maps 3D points and shapes from space B to space A, using corresponding 3D points from the two spaces. The input points must be non-collinear. The FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D function helps to generate a Fixture3D transform using N points from coordinate space A and the same points from coordinate space B. The number of points must be at least 3. To convert points from 3D camera space to robot space, you have to set the coordinates of these N points in both the 3D camera space coordinate system and 3D robot space. As an example, you can use the 4 top corners of the Frustum:

- To know the 3D coordinates of the 4 corners in robot space, use a tactile device.
- To know the 3D coordinates of the 4 corners in 3D camera space, use spreadsheet functions, like PointFromLines3D.

If you want the Fixture3D to convert points from camera space to robot space, set first the points in robot space, and then in camera space. As an example, when you have a Fixture3D structure, you can use a Point3D function to get the picking point in robot space by using the picking point in 3D camera space and the previously computed Fixture3D.

### Inputs

The FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D function has the following syntax: FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D(Point3D A0, Point3D A1, Point3D A2, [Point3D A3,..., Point3D AN], Point3D B0, Point3D B1, Point3D B2, [Point3D B3,..., Point3D BN]) The first N points corresponds to the points in A space, and the other ones corresponding to the physical same points, but in space B.

### Outputs

The FixtureFromPointsToPoints3D function returns a Fixture3D structure.

### Vision Data Access functions

The Structures 3D Vision Data Access functions which create the result table are:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
|  | GetRotation(Fixture3D) Returns the rotation of the Z-axis in degrees, also known as the in-plane rotation. GetTilt(Fixture3D) Returns the tilt angle of the Fixture3D structure in degrees on the Z-axis. GetTiltDirection(Fixture3D) Returns the tilt direction angle of the specified Fixture3D structure in degrees. The angle is measured in the X-Y plane of the original reference coordinate system, and specifies the direction for the projection of the tilted Z-axis onto that plane. GetX(Fixture3D) Returns the X-axis coordinate of the constructed fixture. |
| GetY(Fixture3D) | Returns the Y-axis coordinate of the constructed fixture. |
| GetZ(Fixture3D) | Returns the Z-axis coordinate of the constructed fixture. The Structures 3D Vision Data Access functions are not automatically inserted into the spreadsheet. By default, Fixture3D appears without getters in the cell A21: To display get functions, right click on the Fixture3D cell and select Insert Getters from the dropdown: After you click on Insert Getters, the Structures 3D Vision Data Access functions appear in another Fixture3D structure in the cell A15: |

## Line3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/Line3D.htm`*

The Line3D function allows you to create a fixtured 3D line segment in the point cloud. It returns a Line3D structure containing the settings of the fixtured 3D line segment.

### Inputs

The Line3D function has the following syntax: Line3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Line3D,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Line3D | Specifies the offsets of the 3D line to configure. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1} X0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Y0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Z0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. X1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Y1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Show Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Line3D data structure as the projected 3D line, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the following functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create a result table.

- **X0**：Y0
- **Z0**：X1
- **Y1**：Z1

| ❒Line3D

| GetX(Line3D, 0) | GetY(Line3D, 0) |
| GetZ(Line3D, 0) | GetX(Line3D, 1) |
| GetY(Line3D, 1) | GetZ(Line3D, 1) |

### Vision Data Access functions

The following Structures 3D Vision Data Access functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create the result table:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|

An index value of 0 indicates the first endpoint of the line, while a value of 1 indicates its second endpoint. GetY(Line3D, index) Returns the Y-axis coordinate of the 3D line point specified with the index. An index value of 0 indicates the first endpoint of the line, while a value of 1 indicates its second endpoint. GetZ(Line3D, index) Returns the Z-axis coordinate of the 3D line point specified with the index. An index value of 0 indicates the first endpoint of the line, while a value of 1 indicates its second endpoint. |

The direction of the lines determines which angle the LineToLineAngle3D function measures between the two lines. The following illustrations show how the line direction defines the angle measurement:

### Inputs

Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Line 0 is set to 0. |

| Line3D 1 | Specifies the offsets of the second 3D line. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1} X0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. ## LineToPlaneAngle3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/LineToPlaneAngle3D.htm`*

The LineToPlaneAngle3D function is used to measure the angle between a Line3D structure and a Plane3D structure. It returns the results (that is, the angle value) as an integer in the cell where the function is inserted.

### Inputs

The LineToPlaneAngle3D function has the following syntax: LineToPlaneAngle3D(PointCloud,Line3D,ExternalLine,Plane3D,ExternalPlane,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Line3D | Specifies the offsets of the 3D line structure to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1} X0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. X1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Line is set to 0. |
| External Line | Specifies a reference to the Line3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Line3D structure instead. |
| Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

The measured angle value as an integer type.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the measured angle value is returned by the function.

## LineToRectangleAngles3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/LineToRectangleAngles3D.htm`*

The LineToRectangleAngles3D function measures the angles of the specified Line3D structure relative to the specified Rectangle3D structure. It returns the results (that is, the tilt and tilt direction of the detected angle) in an Angles3D structure.

### Inputs

The LineToRectangleAngles3D function has the following syntax: LineToRectangleAngles3D(PointCloud,Line3D,ExternalLine,Rectangle3D,ExternalRectangle,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Line3D | Specifies the offsets of the 3D line structure to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1} X0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. X1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Line is set to 0. |
| External Line | Specifies a reference to the Line3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Line3D structure instead. |
| Rectangle3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the 3D rectangle of the function. Double-click on the Rectangle3D parameter in the property sheet to adjust the rectangle on the acquisition display. Rectangle3D is offset from the PointCloud origin or the external fixture in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the rectangle along the PointCloud X-axis. SizeY The size of the rectangle along the PointCloud Y-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is only available if you set External Rectangle to 0. |
| External Rectangle | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell for constructing the 3D structure. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Rectangle3D structure of the function. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

An Angles3D data structure containing the angle measurements, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the following functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create a result table.

| Tilt | Tilt Direction |

| ❒Angles3D

| GetTilt(Angles3D) | GetTiltDirection(Angles3D) |

### Vision Data Access functions

The following Angles3D Vision Data Access functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create the result table:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
|  | GetTiltDirection(Angles3D) Returns the tilt direction angle of the specified Angles3D structure in degrees. The angle is measured in the X-Y plane of the original reference coordinate system, and specifies the direction for the projection of the tilted Z-axis onto that plane. GetTilt(Angles3D) Returns the tilt angle of the Angles3D structure in degrees on the Z-axis. |

## MultiBoxRegion3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/MultiBoxRegion3D.htm`*

The MultiBoxRegion3D function allows you to create a Region3D structure that stores up to four fixtured 3D boxes. It returns a Region3D structure containing the settings of the fixtured 3D box(es).

### Inputs

The MultiBoxRegion3D function has the following syntax: MultiBoxRegion3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,NumberOfBoxes,Box3D0,ExternalBox0,Box3D1,ExternalBox1,Box3D2,ExternalBox2,Box3D3,ExternalBox3,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Number of Boxes | Specifies the number of boxes used for specifying the region(s). The value range is 1–4 and the default value is 1 (that is, a single box will be used for specifying the region). Note: If this parameter is set to 1, then only the first Box 3D and External Box parameters will be enabled. |
| Box3D 0 | Specifies the size and position of the (first) 3D box structure to use for specifying the region. It is offset from the origin of the configured Fixture3D structure with the following arguments. SizeX The size of the box along the X-axis of Fixture3D. The value range is 0.001 to inf. SizeY The size of the box along the Y-axis of Fixture3D. The value range is 0.001 to inf. SizeZ The size of the box along the Z-axis of Fixture3D. The value range is 0.001 to inf. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Rotation Specifies the box's in-plane rotation (in degrees) about the Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the box's tilt angle (in degrees) from the Fixture3D Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the box's direction of tilt (in degrees) from the tool's rotated Fixture3D X-axis, about the tool's Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Box 0 is set to 0. |
| External Box 0 | Specifies a reference to a Box3D structure defined in another cell to be used as the (first) region of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Box3D structure for configuring the region. |
| Box3D 1 | Specifies the size and position of the second 3D box structure to use for specifying the region. It is offset from the origin of the configured Fixture3D structure with the following arguments. SizeX The size of the box along the X-axis of Fixture3D. The value range is 0.001 to inf. SizeY The size of the box along the Y-axis of Fixture3D. The value range is 0.001 to inf. SizeZ The size of the box along the Z-axis of Fixture3D. The value range is 0.001 to inf. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Box 1 is set to 0. |

## ParallelPlane3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ParallelPlane3D.htm`*

The ParallelPlane3D function is used to construct a plane parallel to an input plane with the specified offset. It returns the constructed plane as a Plane3D structure.

### Inputs

The ParallelPlane3D function has the following syntax: ParallelPlane3D(PointCloud,Plane3D,ExternalPlane,Offset,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, Tilt Direction} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0 – 180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. |
| Offset | Specifies the signed distance above or below the plane to position the parallel plane. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 1. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane 1 is set to 0. |
| External Plane 1 | Specifies a reference to a Plane3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function as the second 3D plane. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |

## PlaneXY

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/PlaneXY.htm`*

The PlaneXY function is used to quickly construct a Plane3D structure, positioned at the origin and oriented towards the +Z axis. Use this function to construct a plane if you cannot use any reliable features on the point cloud to measure from along the Z-axis. For example, if the configured application is inspecting the top part of a tall object, and the conveyor surface (on which the object is transported) is outside the vision system's field of view, you can use the PlaneXY tool to measure from any height, as long as neither the vision system nor the conveyor has any vertical movement on the Z-axis. Tip: You can construct additional parallel or perpendicular planes by using the fixed plane of this tool, with the ParallelPlane3D and PerpendicularPlane3D functions, respectively. This allows you to use the vision system's FOV features to construct other geometric shapes.

### Inputs

The PlaneXY function has the following syntax: PlaneXY(PointCloud,[Show]) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Inserting the tool into the Spreadsheet returns the configured plane as a Plane3D structure.)

## PlaneXZ

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/PlaneXZ.htm`*

The PlaneXZ function is used to quickly construct a Plane3D structure, positioned at the origin and oriented towards the +Y axis. Use this function to construct a plane if you cannot use any reliable features on the point cloud to measure from along the Y-axis. For example, if the configured application is inspecting the front of a long object, and the opposite end of the object is outside the field of view of the vision system, you can use the PlaneXZ tool to measure length, as long as neither the vision system nor the object has any horizontal movement on the Y-axis. Tip: You can construct additional parallel or perpendicular planes by using the fixed plane of this tool, with the ParallelPlane3D and PerpendicularPlane3D functions, respectively. This allows you to use the FOV features of the vision system to construct other geometric shapes.

### Inputs

The PlaneXZ function has the following syntax: PlaneXZ(PointCloud,[Show]) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Inserting the tool into the Spreadsheet returns the configured plane as a Plane3D structure.

Use this function to construct a plane if you cannot use any reliable features on the point cloud to measure from along the X-axis.
