## PlotArc3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/PlotArc3D.htm`*

The PlotArc3D function allows you to draw an arc in the point cloud by specifying three points in the 3D space (acting as its start, mid- and end points, respectively). It returns a Plot structure containing the settings of the plotted arc.

### Inputs

The PlotArc3D function has the following syntax: PlotBox3D(PointCloud,StartPoint3D,ExternalPoint0,MidPoint3D,ExternalPoint1,EndPoint3D,ExternalPoint2,Name,LineDrawingThickness,Color,Transparency,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| External Point 0 | Specifies a reference to a Point3D structure defined in another cell of the spreadsheet to be used as the first point of the arc. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Point3D structure instead. |
| External Point 1 | Specifies a reference to a Point3D structure defined in another cell of the spreadsheet to be used as the midpoint of the arc. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Point3D structure instead. |
| 1 (Checked) = On (default) | The structure will be displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Start Point3D | Specifies the offset of the 3D point to use as the arc's starting point. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Point 0 is set to 0. |
| Mid Point3D | Specifies the offset of the 3D point to use as the arc's midpoint. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Point 1 is set to 0. |
| End Point3D | Specifies the offset of the 3D point to use as the arc's end point. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Point 2 is set to 0. External Point 2 Specifies a reference to a Point3D structure defined in another cell of the spreadsheet to be used as the end point of the arc. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Point3D structure instead. Name The label of the plotted structure. The configured string appears next to the structure. Line Drawing Thickness Specifies the thickness of the plotted arc's lines. The default value is 5. Color Specifies the color of the plotted graphic. Default: 0x32CD32, LimeGreen; max: 0xFFFFFF. Configure different colors by providing the hexadecimal color code in the formula bar or selecting a color from the color picker on the tool property sheet. |
| Transparency | Specifies the transparency of the drawn arc. The value range of the property is 0 – 100 (from no transparency to complete transparency), and the default value is 0 (meaning no transparency). |
| Show | Selects the display mode. |
| 0 (Unchecked) = Off | The structure will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Plot structure that allows you to modify the plotted arc.

Results

When inserted into a cell, a ❒Plot structure is created, containing the settings of the arc drawn in the point cloud when the job is Online.

## PlotBox3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/PlotBox3D.htm`*

The PlotBox3D function allows you to draw a Box3D structure by defining its dimensions, offset and rotation. It returns a Plot structure containing the settings of the plotted box.

### Inputs

The PlotBox3D function has the following syntax: PlotBox3D(PointCloud,Box3D,ExternalBox,Name,Color,Transparency,ShowAxisIndicator,ShowDirectionIndicator,DirectionIndicatorAxis,ModelMode,LineDrawingThickness,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 (Checked) = On (default) | The structure will be displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Box3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the 3D rectangle of the function. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the box along the X-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeY The size of the box along the Y-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeZ The size of the box along the Z-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation of the box (in degrees) about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle of the box (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the tilt direction of the box (in degrees) from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Box is set to 0. External Box Specifies a reference to a Box3D structure defined in another cell of the spreadsheet to be used for plotting. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Box3D structure. Name The label of the plotted structure. The configured string appears next to the structure. |
| Color | Specifies the color of the wireframe or surface, depending on the selected Model Mode. Default: 0x32CD32, LimeGreen; max: 0xFFFFFF. Configure different colors by providing the hexadecimal color code in the formula bar or selecting a color from the color picker on the tool property sheet. Note: If you set the Model Mode parameter to Solid with Wireframe, then the wireframe will be black regardless of the value of this setting. |
| Transparency | Specifies the transparency of the drawn structure or its elements, depending on the selected Model Mode. The value range of the property is 0 – 100 (from no transparency to complete transparency), and the default value is 0 (meaning no transparency). |
| Show Axis Indicator | Shows the axis indicator for the plotted structure. This parameter is disabled by default. |
| Show Direction Indicator | Shows the direction indicator on the axis selected with the Direction Indicator Axis parameter. This parameter is disabled by default. |
| Direction Indicator Axis | Specifies which axis to show the direction of with the Direction Indicator. By default, the X-axis direction is indicated. |
| Model Mode | Specifies how the plotted box will be drawn in the point cloud: <br>- Points: Only the corner points of the plotted box will be drawn. <br>- Wireframe: The plotted box will be drawn as a wireframe only, its surfaces being completely transparent. This is the default setting. <br>- Solid: The plotted box will be drawn with its surfaces being completely solid. <br>- Solid with Wireframe: The plotted box will be drawn with solid surfaces, with its wireframe toned in black color. |
| Line Drawing Thickness | Specifies the thickness of the wireframe lines. This setting is available only if the Model Mode parameter is set to Wireframe or Solid with Wireframe, and its default value is 5 with a range between 1 to 10. |
| Show | Selects the display mode. |
| 0 (Unchecked) = Off | The structure will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Plot structure that allows you to modify the plotted Box3D structure.

Results

When inserted into a cell, a ❒Plot structure is created, containing the settings of the 3D box drawn in the point cloud when the job is Online.

| External Cylinder | Specifies a reference to a Cylinder3D structure defined in another cell of the spreadsheet to be used for plotting the 3D cylinder. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Cylinder3D structure. |
| Name | The label of the plotted structure. The configured string appears next to the structure. |
| Color | Specifies the color of the wireframe or surface, depending on the selected Model Mode. Default: 0x32CD32, LimeGreen; max: 0xFFFFFF. Configure different colors by providing the hexadecimal color code in the formula bar or selecting a color from the color picker on the tool property sheet. Note: If you set the Model Mode parameter to Solid with Wireframe, then the wireframe will be black regardless of the value of this setting. |
| Transparency | Specifies the transparency of the drawn structure or its elements, depending on the selected Model Mode. The value range of the property is 0 – 100 (from no transparency to complete transparency), and the default value is 0 (meaning no transparency). |
| Model Mode | Specifies how the cylinder will be drawn in the point cloud: <br>- Points: This setting draws the cylinder's top and bottom surfaces and its center Z-axis by points. <br>- Wireframe: The cylinder will be drawn as a wireframe only, its surfaces being completely transparent. This is the default setting. <br>- Solid: The region will be drawn with its surfaces being completely solid. <br>- Solid with Wireframe: The region will be drawn with solid surfaces, with its wireframe toned in black color. |
| Line Drawing Thickness | Specifies the thickness of the wireframe lines. This setting is available only if the Model Mode parameter is set to Wireframe or Solid with Wireframe, and its default value is 5 with a range between 1 to 10. |
| Show | Selects the display mode. |
| 0 (Unchecked) = Off | The structure will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Plot structure that allows you to modify the plotted Cylinder3D structure.

Results

When inserted into a cell, a ❒Plot structure is created, containing the settings of the 3D cylinder drawn in the point cloud when the job is Online.

## PlotExternalRegion3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/PlotExternalRegion3D.htm`*

The PlotExternalRegion3D function allows you to draw a Region3D structure by referencing an existing 3D region such as a Region3D, Box3D, Cylinder3D,Plane3D, or MultiBoxRegion3D configured in another spreadsheet cell. The PlotExternalRegion3D function returns a Plot structure containing the settings of the drawn Region3D.

### Inputs

The PlotExternalRegion3D function has the following syntax: PlotExternalRegion3D(PointCloud,ExternalRegion,Color,Transparency,ShowAxisIndicator,ShowDirectionIndicator,DirectionIndicatorAxis,ModelMode,LineDrawingThickness,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 (Checked) = On (default) | The structure will be displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell of the spreadsheet to be used for plotting the Region3D structure. Note: Leaving this setting on 0 (OFF) results in the function returning an error once set up. |
| Color | Specifies the color of the wireframe or surface, depending on the selected Model Mode. Default: 0x32CD32, LimeGreen; max: 0xFFFFFF. Configure different colors by providing the hexadecimal color code in the formula bar or selecting a color from the color picker on the tool property sheet. Note: If you set the Model Mode parameter to Solid with Wireframe, then the wireframe will be black regardless of the value of this setting. |
| Transparency | Specifies the transparency of the drawn structure or its elements, depending on the selected Model Mode. The value range of the property is 0 – 100 (from no transparency to complete transparency), and the default value is 0 (meaning no transparency). |
| Show Axis Indicator | Shows the axis indicator for the plotted structure. This parameter is disabled by default. Note: This parameter is only available if the External Region parameter points to a Box3D structure. |
| Show Direction Indicator | Shows the direction indicator on the axis selected with the Direction Indicator Axis parameter. This parameter is disabled by default. Note: This parameter is only available if the External Region parameter points to a Box3D structure. |
| Direction Indicator Axis | Specifies which axis to show the direction of with the Direction Indicator. By default, the X-axis direction is indicated. Note: This parameter is only available if the External Region parameter points to a Box3D structure. |
| Model Mode | Specifies how the region is drawn in the point cloud: <br>- Points: Only the corner points of the region are drawn. <br>- Wireframe: The region is drawn as a wireframe only, its surfaces being completely transparent. This is the default setting. <br>- Solid: The region is drawn with its surfaces being completely solid. <br>- Solid with Wireframe: The region is drawn with solid surfaces, with its wireframe toned in black color. |
| Line Drawing Thickness | Specifies the thickness of the wireframe lines. This setting is available only if the Model Mode parameter is set to Wireframe or Solid with Wireframe, and its default value is 5 with a range between 1 to 10. |
| Show | Selects the display mode. |
| 0 (Unchecked) = Off | The structure will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Plot structure that allows you to modify the plotted 3D region.

Results

When inserted into a cell, a ❒Plot structure is created, containing the settings of the 3D region drawn in the point cloud when the job is Online.

## PlotFixture3D

The PlotFixture3D function allows you to draw a 3D fixture. It returns a Plot structure containing the settings of the drawn 3D fixture.

The PlotFixture3D function has the following syntax: PlotFixture3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Name,Color,Transparency,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 (Checked) = On (default) | The structure will be displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |

| Color | Specifies the color of the fixture's name (configured with the Name parameter). |
| Transparency | Specifies the transparency of the fixture's label (configured with the Name parameter). The value range of the property is 0 – 100 (from no transparency to complete transparency), and the default value is 0 (meaning no transparency). |
| Show | Selects the display mode. |
| 0 (Unchecked) = Off | The structure will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Plot structure that allows you to modify the plotted Fixture3D structure.

Results

When inserted into a cell, a ❒Plot structure is created, containing the settings of the 3D fixture drawn in the point cloud when the job is Online.

The PlotLine3D function allows you to draw a Line3D structure by defining the X, Y and Z-axis position of its starting and end points. The function supports drawing arrows and regular lines as well. It returns a Plot structure containing the settings of the plotted box.

### Inputs

The PlotLine3D function has the following syntax: PlotLine3D(PointCloud,Line3D,ExternalLine,Name,LineDrawingThickness,Color,Transparency,LineDrawingStyle,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 (Checked) = On (default) | The structure will be displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Line3D | Specifies the offsets of the 3D line structure to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1} X0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. X1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Line is set to 0. |
| External Line | Specifies a reference to the Line3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Line3D structure instead. |
| Name | The label of the plotted structure. The configured string appears next to the structure. |
| Line Drawing Thickness | Specifies the thickness of the line. The default value is 5. |
| Color | Specifies the color of the plotted graphic. Default: 0x32CD32, LimeGreen; max: 0xFFFFFF. Configure different colors by providing the hexadecimal color code in the formula bar or selecting a color from the color picker on the tool property sheet. |
| Transparency | Specifies the transparency of the drawn line. The value range of the property is 0 – 100 (from no transparency to complete transparency), and the default value is 0 (meaning no transparency). |
| Line Drawing Style | Specifies the type of line that will be drawn: <br>- Start Arrow: Draws an arrow, with the arrowhead located at the starting point of the line. <br>- End Arrow: Draws an arrow, with the arrowhead located at the end point of the line. <br>- Both Arrows: Draws a left-right arrow. <br>- Regular: Draws a regular line with no arrowhead. |
| Show | Selects the display mode. |
| 0 (Unchecked) = Off | The structure will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Plot structure that allows you to modify the plotted Line3D structure.

Results

When inserted into a cell, a ❒Plot structure is created, containing the settings of the 3D line drawn in the point cloud when the job is Online.

Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. Note: You can use Plane3D to mask data for training. The Plane3D function prevents the tool from taking any points that belong to that plane and are within the ROI. External Plane Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. | Name | Specifies the value of the string. You can enter either a text string, or a reference to an existing text string. |
| Point3D | Specifies the offset of the 3D point to use. It is offset from the PointCloud (or Fixture3D, if Fixture Reference is enabled) origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Point is set to 0. |
| External Point | Specifies a reference to a Point3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Point3D structure. |
| Color | Specifies the color of the plotted graphic. Default: 0x32CD32, LimeGreen; max: 0xFFFFFF. Configure different colors by providing the hexadecimal color code in the formula bar or selecting a color from the color picker on the tool property sheet. |
| Transparency | Specifies the transparency of the string. The value range of the property is 0 – 100 (from no transparency to complete transparency), and the default value is 0 (meaning no transparency). |
| Show | Selects the display mode. |
| 0 (Unchecked) = Off | The structure will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Plot structure that allows you to modify the plotted string.

Results

When inserted into a cell, a ❒Plot structure is created, containing the settings of the string drawn in the point cloud when the job is Online.

## Point3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/Point3D.htm`*

The Point3D function allows you to create a fixtured 3D point in the point cloud. It returns a Point3D structure containing the settings of the fixtured 3D point.

### Inputs

The Point3D function has the following syntax: Plane3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Point3D,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Point3D | Specifies the offset of the 3D point to use. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Point is set to 0. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Point3D data structure containing the constructed 3D point, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the following functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create a result table.

X
Y
Z
| ❒Point3D

GetX(Point3D)
GetY(Point3D)
GetZ(Point3D)

## PointFromLineAndPlane3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/PointFromLineAndPlane3D.htm`*

The PointFromLineAndPlane3D function is used to construct a 3D point from a Plane3D structure and the Line3D structure intersecting it. The function returns the constructed point as a Point3D structure.

### Inputs

The PointFromLineAndPlane3D function has the following syntax: PointFromLineAndPlane3D(PointCloud,Line3D,ExternalLine,Plane3D,ExternalPlane,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Line3D | Specifies the offsets of the 3D line structure to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1} X0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. X1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Line is set to 0. |
| External Line | Specifies a reference to the Line3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Line3D structure instead. |
| Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

Returns

Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Line is set to 0. |

## PointToPlane3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/PointToPlane3D.htm`*

The PointToPlane3D function is used to measure the angle and distance between a Point3D structure and a Plane3D structure. It returns the calculated distance and angle values in a Dist3D structure, which can be referenced with Dist3D Vision Data Access functions.

### Inputs

The PointToPlane3D function has the following syntax: PointToPlane3D(PointCloud,Point3D,ExternalPoint,Plane3D,ExternalPlane,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Point3D | Specifies the offset of the 3D point to use. It is offset from the PointCloud (or Fixture3D, if Fixture Reference is enabled) origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Point is set to 0. |
| External Point | Specifies a reference to a Point3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Point3D structure. |
| Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Dist3D data structure containing distance and angle measurement.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the following functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create a result table.

- **X0**：Y0
- **Z0**：X1
- **Y1**：Z1
- **AngleX**：AngleY
- **AngleZ**：Distance

| ❒Dist3D

| GetX(Dist3D, 0) | GetY(Dist3D, 0) |
| GetZ(Dist3D, 0) | GetX(Dist3D, 1) |
| GetY(Dist3D, 1) | GetZ(Dist3D, 1) |
| GetAngleX(Dist3D) | GetAngleY(Dist3D) |
| GetAngleZ(Dist3D) | GetDistance(Dist3D) |

| Function | Description |
|---|---|

GetAngleZ(Dist3D) Returns the rotation between the 3D point and the plane about the Z-axis. GetDistance(Dist3D) Returns the distance calculated between the 3D point and the plane. GetX(Dist3D, index) Returns the X-axis coordinate of the center point of the shape specified with the index number. <br>- index = 0: First shape. <br>- index = 1: Second shape. |

## ProfileArea3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ProfileArea3D.htm`*

The ProfileArea3D function allows you to measure the area between a profile and a user-defined line in a Profile3D structure. The ProfileArea3D function requires an existing Profile3D structure as input. You can also define a Region of Interest within the profile to narrow down the analysis and provide more specific results.

3D Point Cloud with ProfileArea3D
Profile View
The ProfileArea3D function also allows you to use an external ProfileFixture3D input, which ensures that the function measures the same profile area for each acquisition. The ProfileArea3D function can use the profile fixture to align the Profile Region and the Profile Line, and produce consistent results regardless of positioning inconsistencies in the acquisition. The ProfileArea3D function produces a measurement value in square units, as well as Point3D structures for minimum and maximum points on both profile axes.

### Inputs

The ProfileArea3D function has the following syntax: ProfileArea3D(Profile3D, ProfileFixture3D, ExternalProfileFixture3D, ProfileRegion, AreaMeasurementMode, FillMarkedGaps, GapSizeThreshold, NudgeDistance, ProfileLine, ExternalLine, Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| External Profile | Specifies the Profile3D structure to use. |
| Profile Fixture | Specifies the coordinates defining the profile fixture. It is offset from the profile origin in the following format with the following arguments: {Xp, Zp, Angle} X Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin. Angle Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Y-axis of the profile origin. The value range is 0 to 180. Note: This parameter is only available if you set External Profile Fixture to 0. |
| External Profile Fixture | Specifies a reference to a ProfileFixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the ProfileFixture3D cell as the profile fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal profile fixture of the function instead. |
| Profile Region | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the Profile Region of the function. The Profile Region is offset from the profile origin or the external fixture in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeXp, SizeZp, Xp, Zp, Angle} SizeXp The size of the Profile Region along the profile X-axis. SizeZp The size of the Profile Region along the profile Z-axis. Xp Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin. Zp Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin. Area Measurement Mode Specifies the mode of measurement: <br>- Above(0) <br>- measures the profile area above the profile line. <br>- Below(1) <br>- measures the profile area below the profile line. <br>- Above plus Below(2) <br>- measures the profile area both above and below the profile line. <br>- Above minus Below(3) <br>- measures the profile area above the profile line, and subtracts the profile area below the profile line. Fill Marked Gaps Enables or disables filling gaps in the profile. Gap Size Threshold Specifies the maximum gap size threshold for filling gaps in the profile. Note: This parameter is only available if you enable Fill Marked Gaps. Nudge Distance Specifies a Zp-axis offset for the profile line. Profile Line Specifies the start and end point coordinates for the profile line to use: Xp0 X-axis coordinate value for the start point of the profile line in the profile coordinate space. Zp0 Z-axis coordinate value for the start point of the profile line in the profile coordinate space. Xp1 X-axis coordinate value for the end point of the profile line in the profile coordinate space. Zp1 Z-axis coordinate value for the end point of the profile line in the profile coordinate space. Note: This parameter is available only if External Line is set to 0. |
| External Line | Specifies a reference to a Line3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the Line3D structure as the profile line. Set to 0 (OFF) to manually define the profile line coordinates instead. Note: Profile Fixture and External Profile Fixture settings do not affect External Line references. Only manually defined profile lines use the profile fixture coordinates. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

An area measurement value, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the following functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create a result table:

Area
Min Xp Point
Max Xp Point
Min Zp Point
Max Zp Point
| ❒ProfileArea3D

GetArea(Profile3D)
| ❒Point3D

| | ❒Point3D |
| | ❒Point3D |
| | ❒Point3D |

## ProfileExtractCircle3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ProfileExtractCircle3D.htm`*

The ProfileExtractCircle3D function allows you to extract circles from a profile. The ProfileExtractCircle3D function requires an existing Profile3D structure as input. You can also define a Region of Interest within the profile to narrow down the analysis provide more accurate results. The circle extraction function creates a circle that best fits the profile points in the defined region.

3D Point Cloud with ProfileExtractCircle3D
Profile View
The ProfileExtractCircle3D function also allows you to use an external ProfileFixture3D input, which ensures that the function extracts the same profile feature for each acquisition. The ProfileExtractCircle3D function can use the profile fixture to align the Region of Interest in the profile, and produce consistent results regardless of positioning inconsistencies in the acquisition. The ProfileExtractCircle3D function produces a Circle3D structure that you can use as input for other functions.

### Inputs

The ProfileExtractCircle3D function has the following syntax: ProfileExtractCircle3D(Profile3D, ProfileFixture3D, ExternalProfileFixture3D, ProfileRegion, FitMode, OutlierDistanceThreshold, UseSpecifiedRadius, Radius, Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| External Profile | Specifies the Profile3D structure to use. |
| Profile Fixture | Specifies the coordinates defining the profile fixture. It is offset from the profile origin in the following format with the following arguments: {Xp, Zp, Angle} X Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin. Angle Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Y-axis of the profile origin. The value range is 0 to 180. Note: This parameter is only available if you set External Profile Fixture to 0. |
| External Profile Fixture | Specifies a reference to a ProfileFixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the ProfileFixture3D cell as the profile fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal profile fixture of the function instead. |
| Profile Region | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the Profile Region of the function. The Profile Region is offset from the profile origin or the external fixture in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeXp, SizeZp, Xp, Zp, Angle} SizeXp The size of the Profile Region along the profile X-axis. SizeZp The size of the Profile Region along the profile Z-axis. Xp Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin. Zp Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin. Angle Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the profile Z-axis. The value range is 0 to 180. Fit Mode Specifies the fit mode: <br>- Quick(0) <br>- uses all profile points in the defined region to find the best fit in a single pass. <br>- High-Accuracy(1) <br>- uses a two-pass fitting process to find the best fit, with the Outlier Outliers are the subset of input points that fall outside a specified distance from a fitted geometric model, such as a sphere or cylinder. These points do not meet the user-defined distance threshold and are excluded from the model. A high number of outliers can indicate noise in the data or a poor model fit. Distance Threshold acting as a filter for the second pass. |
| Outlier Distance Threshold | Specifies the threshold for filtering outliers when using High-Accuracy fit mode. Note: This parameter is only available if you set Fit Mode to High-Accuracy. |
| Use Specified Radius | Enables or disables manual definition of the radius for the extracted circle. |
| Radius | Specifies the radius of the extracted circle. Note: This parameter is only available if you enable Use Specified Radius. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Circle3D data structure containing the extracted circle, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the following functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create a result table:

- **Circle**：Radius
- **Center**：X
- **Y**：Z

The ProfileExtractCornerPoint3D function produces a Point3D structure for each extracted corner point, that you can use as input for other functions.

### Inputs

The ProfileExtractCornerPoint3D function has the following syntax: ProfileExtractCornerPoint3D(Profile3D, ProfileFixture3D, ExternalProfileFixture3D, ProfileRegion, CornerType, MinCornerAngle, MaxCornerAngle, SegmentLength, SegmentSeparation, SortKey, SortOrder, Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| External Profile | Specifies the Profile3D structure to use. |
| Profile Fixture | Specifies the coordinates defining the profile fixture. It is offset from the profile origin in the following format with the following arguments: {Xp, Zp, Angle} X Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin. Angle Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Y-axis of the profile origin. The value range is 0 to 180. Note: This parameter is only available if you set External Profile Fixture to 0. |
| External Profile Fixture | Specifies a reference to a ProfileFixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the ProfileFixture3D cell as the profile fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal profile fixture of the function instead. |
| Profile Region | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the Profile Region of the function. The Profile Region is offset from the profile origin or the external fixture in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeXp, SizeZp, Xp, Zp, Angle} SizeXp The size of the Profile Region along the profile X-axis. SizeZp The size of the Profile Region along the profile Z-axis. Xp Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin. Zp Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin. Angle Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the profile Z-axis. The value range is 0 to 180. Corner Type Specifies the corner type to be extracted: <br>- Convex(0) <br>- extracts only convex corner points. <br>- Concave(1) <br>- extracts only concave corner points. <br>- Any(2) <br>- extracts both convex and concave corner points. |
| Minimum Corner Angle | Specifies the minimum angle in degrees for the function to identify a corner point. The value range is 0 to 180. |
| Maximum Corner Angle | Specifies the maximum angle in degrees for the function to identify a corner point. The value range is 0 to 180. Segment Length Specifies the length of the line segments that define the angle in a corner point. Default is 1. Segment Separation Specifies the amount of separation allowed between the line segments that define the angle in a corner point. Default is 0. Sort Key Specifies the way that the function indexes the extracted corner points and sorts the output table: <br>- None(0) <br>- Point Xp(2) <br>- sorts the corners by coordinate value on the Xp-axis. <br>- Point Zp(3) <br>- sorts the corners by coordinate value on the Zp-axis. <br>- Corner Angle(4) <br>- sorts the corners by angle. <br>- Tangent Angle(5) <br>- sorts the corners by the angle between the tangent line of the corner and the Xp-axis. |
| Sort Order | Specifies the order in which the function indexes the extracted corner points and sorts the output table: <br>- Descending(0) <br>- Ascending(1) |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |

## ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D.htm`*

The ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D function allows you to extract edge points from a profile where a user-defined reference line and the profile intersect with each other. The ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D function requires an existing Profile3D structure as input. You can use the function to extract rising edge points, falling edge points, or both. The function extracts all edge points of the input profile that fit the defined criteria as individual Point3D structures.

3D Point Cloud with ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D
Profile View
The ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D function also allows you to use an external ProfileFixture3D input, which ensures that the function extracts the same profile feature for each acquisition.The ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D function can use the profile fixture to align the intersecting line in the profile, and produce consistent results regardless of positioning inconsistencies in the acquisition. The ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D function produces a Point3D structure for each extracted corner point, that you can use as input for other functions.

### Inputs

The ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D function has the following syntax: ProfileExtractEdgePoint3D(Profile3D, ProfileFixture3D, ExternalProfileFixture3D, ProfileLine, ExternalProfileLine, EdgeType, SortKey, SortOrder, Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| External Profile | Specifies the Profile3D structure to use. |
| Profile Fixture | Specifies the coordinates defining the profile fixture. It is offset from the profile origin in the following format with the following arguments: {Xp, Zp, Angle} X Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin. Angle Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Y-axis of the profile origin. The value range is 0 to 180. Note: This parameter is only available if you set External Profile Fixture to 0. |
| External Profile Fixture | Specifies a reference to a ProfileFixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the ProfileFixture3D cell as the profile fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal profile fixture of the function instead. |
| Profile Line | Specifies the offset of the two end points for the intersecting reference line of the function. The profile line is offset from the profile origin or the external fixture in the following format with the following arguments: {Xp0, Zp0, Xp1, Zp1} Xp0 The X-axis coordinate value for the first end point of the profile line. Zp0 The Z-axis coordinate value for the first end point of the profile line. Xp1 The X-axis coordinate value for the second end point of the profile line. Zp1 The Z-axis coordinate value for the second end point of the profile line. Note: This parameter is only available if you set External Line to 0. |
| External Line | Specifies a reference to a Line3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the profile line of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal line of the function instead. Note: The External Line parameter is independent from the External Fixture setting. |
| Edge Type | Specifies type of edge points to be extracted: <br>- Rising(0) <br>- the Z coordinate value of the profile before the point is lower than the Z coordinate value of the profile after the point. <br>- Falling(1) <br>- the Z coordinate value of the profile before the point is higher than the Z coordinate value of the profile after the point. <br>- Any(2) <br>- the function recognizes both rising and falling edge points. |
| Sort Key | Specifies the way that the function indexes the extracted edge points and sorts the output table: <br>- None(0) <br>- Point Xp(2) <br>- sorts the edge points by coordinate value on the Xp-axis. <br>- Point Zp(3) <br>- sorts the edge points by coordinate value on the Zp axis. |
| Sort Order | Specifies the order in which the function indexes the extracted edge points and sorts the output table: <br>- Descending(0) <br>- Ascending(1) |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A ProfileEdgePoints3D data structure, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

## ProfileExtractLine3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ProfileExtractLine3D.htm`*

The ProfileExtractLine3D function allows you to extract a straight line from a profile based on the profile points located inside the defined region. The ProfileExtractLine3D function requires an existing Profile3D structure as input.

3D Point Cloud with ProfileExtractLine3D
Profile View
The ProfileExtractLine3D function also allows you to use an external ProfileFixture3D input, which ensures that the function extracts the same profile feature for each acquisition. The ProfileExtractLine3D function can use the profile fixture to align the intersecting line in the profile, and produce consistent results regardless of positioning inconsistencies in the acquisition. The ProfileExtractLine3D function produces a Line3D structure that you can use as input for other functions.

### Inputs

The ProfileExtractLine3D function has the following syntax: ProfileExtractLine3D(Profile3D, ProfileFixture3D, ExternalProfileFixture3D, Region3D, FitMode, Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| External Profile | Specifies the Profile3D structure to use. |
| Profile Fixture | Specifies the coordinates defining the profile fixture. It is offset from the profile origin in the following format with the following arguments: {Xp, Zp, Angle} X Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin. Angle Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Y-axis of the profile origin. The value range is 0 to 180. Note: This parameter is only available if you set External Profile Fixture to 0. |
| External Profile Fixture | Specifies a reference to a ProfileFixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the ProfileFixture3D cell as the profile fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal profile fixture of the function instead. |
| Profile Region | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the Profile Region of the function. The Profile Region is offset from the profile origin or the external fixture in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeXp, SizeZp, Xp, Zp, Angle} SizeXp The size of the Profile Region along the profile X-axis. SizeZp The size of the Profile Region along the profile Z-axis. Xp Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin. Zp Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin. Angle Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the profile Z-axis. The value range is 0 to 180. Fit Mode Specifies the fit mode: <br>- Quick(0) <br>- uses all profile points in the defined region to find the best fit in a single pass. <br>- High-Accuracy(1) <br>- uses a two-pass fitting process to find the best fit, with the Outlier Outliers are the subset of input points that fall outside a specified distance from a fitted geometric model, such as a sphere or cylinder. These points do not meet the user-defined distance threshold and are excluded from the model. A high number of outliers can indicate noise in the data or a poor model fit. Distance Threshold acting as a filter for the second pass. |

The ProfileFixtureFromPoint3D function requires a Profile3D structure and a Point3D structure as input. Zp Z-axis coordinate value for the profile point in the profile coordinate space. Note: This parameter is available only if External Point is set to 0. |
| External Point | Specifies a reference to a Point3D structure defined in another cell. Set to 0 (OFF) to manually define the Point3D coordinates instead. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |

## ProfileFlatness3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ProfileFlatness3D.htm`*

The ProfileFlatness3D function allows you to measure the flatness of a profile in a Profile3D structure. The ProfileFlatness3D function requires an existing Profile3D structure as input. You can also define a Region of Interest within the profile to narrow down the analysis and provide more specific results.

3D Point Cloud with ProfileFlatness3D
Profile View
The ProfileFlatness3D function also allows you to use an external ProfileFixture3D input, which ensures that the function measures the same profile flatness for each acquisition. The ProfileFlatness3D function can use the profile fixture to align the Profile Region, and produce consistent results regardless of positioning inconsistencies in the acquisition.

### Inputs

The ProfileFlatness3D function has the following syntax: ProfileFlatness3D(Profile3D, ProfileFixture3D, ExternalProfileFixture3D, ProfileRegion, FlatnessMode, Show)

Parameter

Description
External Profile

Specifies the Profile3D structure to use.

Profile Fixture

Specifies the coordinates defining the profile fixture. It is offset from the profile origin in the following format with the following arguments: {Xp, Zp, Angle}

- **Xp**：Offset on the Xp-axis from the profile origin.
- **Zp**：Offset on the Zp-axis from the profile origin.
- **Angle**：Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Yp-axis of the profile origin. The value range is 0 to 180.

Note: This parameter is only available if you set External Profile Fixture to 0.

External Profile Fixture
Specifies a reference to a ProfileFixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the ProfileFixture3D cell as the profile fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal profile fixture of the function instead.

Profile Region
Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the Profile Region of the function. The Profile Region is offset from the profile origin or the external fixture in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeXp, SizeZp, Xp, Zp, Angle}

SizeXp
The size of the Profile Region along the profile X-axis.
SizeZp
The size of the Profile Region along the profile Z-axis.
Xp
Offset on the X-axis from the profile origin.
Zp
Offset on the Z-axis from the profile origin.
Angle
Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the profile Z-axis. The value range is 0 to 180.
Flatness Mode
Specifies the mode of flatness measurement:

- Least Squares(0) - minimizes the sum of the squared residuals for all the measurement points.
- Minimum Zone(1) - determines two parallel lines enclosing the profile with the least separation. The Minimum Zone flatness measurement mode provides a more accurate definition of flatness, but can take more processing time than the Least Squares mode.

Show

Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image.

0 = hide all (default)

All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet.

| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |

2 = input and result graphics

The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times.

### Outputs

Returns

A flatness value, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the following functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create a result table:

Flatness
Point Above
Point Below
Line Above
Line Below
| ❒ProfileFlatness3D

GetFlatness(Profile3D)
| ❒Point3D

| | ❒Point3D |
| | ❒Line3D |
| | ❒Line3D |

## ProjectionLineOnPlane3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/ProjectionLineOnPlane3D.htm`*

The ProjectionLineOnPlane3D function constructs a 3D line segment from the projection of the specified input 3D line segment structure onto the specified input plane. The constructed line segment is returned as a Line3D structure.

### Inputs

(The ProjectionLineOnPlane3D function has the following syntax: ProjectionLineOnPlane3D(PointCloud,Line3D,ExternalLine,Plane3D,ExternalPlane,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The constructed line will be displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Line3D | Specifies the offsets of the 3D line structure to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1} X0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z0 Offset of the 3D line's starting point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. X1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z1 Offset of the 3D line's ending point on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Note: This parameter is available only if External Line is set to 0. |
| External Line | Specifies a reference to the Line3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Line3D structure instead. |
| Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input point cloud, the region of interest, and the constructed line will be displayed at all times. |

Returns

A Line3D data structure as the projected 3D line, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/Rectangle3D.htm`*

The Rectangle3D function has the following syntax: Rectangle3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Rectangle3D,Show)

| Parameter | Description |

| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |

It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The rectangle's size along the Fixture3D X-axis. The value range is 0.001 to inf. SizeY The rectangle's size along the Fixture3D Y-axis. The value range is 0.001 to inf. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation (in degrees) about the tool's Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the tool's Fixture3D Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the tool's rotated Fixture3D X-axis, about the tool's Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Show Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |

## Region3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/Region3D.htm`*

The Region3D function allows you to create a fixtured 3D region in the shape of an annular cylinder slice. The function returns a Region3D structure containing the settings of the fixtured 3D region. The EditRegion3D, Region3DFromRegion2D, and CompRegion3DFromCompRegion2D functions also return a Region3D structure. The shape returned by the Region3D function is designed specifically to support the ExtractCircle3D and ExtractRadialCrossSections3D functions, which require this shape as input. However, you can use the output of this function with any tool that requires a Region3D input. For 3D tools that require a Box3D input, you can use the GetBoundingBox function on the Region3D output to get a Box3D structure that fits the Region3D shape. Region3D is equivalent to a Box when the value of the Curve parameter is 0. The following diagrams show an annular cylinder slice, a shape produced by the Region3D function, placed in a coordinate system:

Top View
Side View
Isometric View
To use the Region3D function:

- Drag and drop the Region3D function to the Spreadsheet.
- In the property sheet that pops up, double-click the Region3D parameter to open the interactive display, and adjust the ROI shape projected onto the acquisition display. Alternatively, you can expand the Region3D settings and define the parameters manually.
- Click OK to finalize the settings.

### Inputs

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Region3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle of the 3D region. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, Curve, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} |
| SizeX | When Curve is not 0, SizeX is the length of the Region3D structure along a radius that is the mean of the inner and outer radii of the annular cylinder slice. When Curve is 0, SizeX is the size of the Region3D along the X-axis of the structure. |
| SizeY | When Curve is not 0, SizeY is the difference between the outer and inner radii of the annular cylinder slice. When Curve is 0, SizeY is the size of the Region3D along the Y-axis of the structure. SizeZ The size of the region along the Z-axis of the structure. Curve The angle between the radial edges of the annular slice. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation of the 3D region (in degrees) around the Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range are normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle of the 3D region (in degrees) from the Fixture3D Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the tilt direction of the 3D region (in degrees) from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis, around the Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range are normalized to the allowed range. Show Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | Only the input graphics are displayed. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Box3D structure.

Results

- **SizeX**：SizeY
- **SizeZ**：Curve

| GetSizeZ(Region3D) | Returns the size of the Region3D structure along the Z-axis. GetCurve(Region3D) Returns the angle-of-curvature value in clockwise degrees for the annular slice shape of the Region3D structure. ## Region3DFromRegion2D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/Region3DFromRegion2D.htm`*

The Region3DFromRegion2D function allows you to construct a Region3D structure from a specified two-dimensional Region structure. To use the Region3DFromRegion2D function:

- Drag and drop the Region3DFromRegion2D function into the Spreadsheet.

- Check the Auto Compute Z Range checkbox, or manually adjust the Z center offset and height of the Region3D output structure. The acquisition display shows a preview of the Region3D structure.

External Region Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell for constructing the 3D structure. Auto Compute Z Range Enables or disables automatic Z range computing for the Region3D structure. Z Center Specifies the offset of the Region3D Z-axis center from the point cloud origin, in millimeters. Height Specifies the height of the Region3D structure, in millimeters. Show Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |

GetSizeZ(Region3D) Returns the size of the structure along the Z-axis. GetCurve(Region3D) Returns the angle-of-curvature value, in clockwise degrees. GetX(Region3D) Returns the X-axis coordinate of the specified structure's center point. |

## SetHeightColorRange

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/SetHeightColorRange.htm`*

The SetHeightColorRange function allows you to set the height color range used in the 3D view. It returns a HeightColor3D structure containing the minimum and maximum height (dimension Z) of the color range. If you are not using a SetHeightColorRange function, height color range is automatically computed based on the acquired detection zone for each point cloud. For old point clouds where this information was not stored, a predefined range is used instead. Note: This function can use the Box3D orientation to determine the gradient direction using the Directional mode. To use the SetHeightColorRange function:

- Drag and drop the SetHeightColorRange function to the Spreadsheet.
- In the property sheet that pops up, choose a Height color mode:
- Directional Mode: Use a Box3D to define the height of the color range and direction. Double-click the Box3D parameter to open the interactive display. Adjust the ROI shape on the display. Alternatively, you can expand the Box3D settings and define the parameters manually. The Z range is relative to the Box3D, so the minimum value of the range is always 0 and the highest value is equal to the box SizeZ. The dimensions X and Y have no effect on the result. Note: You can use boxes produced by other 3D tools, such as ExtractBlob3D, to automatically adjust the color based on the computed box from one acquisition to the next.
- Z Range Mode: Define the height color range with the Minimum Z and Maximum Z parameters.
- Click OK to finalize the settings.

### Inputs

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Height color mode | Selects the height color mode: |
| Directional | Applies the height color using a Box3D. The range is equal to SizeZ of the Box3D. The local +Z axis of the Box3D defines the gradient direction. The color bar in the 3D viewer shows "Z Box (mm)" and the range is from 0 to the height of the box. |
| Z Range | Applies the height color based on the Z range that you define with the Minimum Z and the Maximum Z parameters in the Property Sheet. The +Z world axis defines the gradient direction. The color bar shows "Z world (mm)" and the range is from Minimum Z to Maximum Z. Note: You can only use one mode at a time. If you choose Directional mode, the Z Range mode properties are disabled. The same happens if you choose Z Range mode. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. Note: This parameter is available only in Directional mode. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. Note: This parameter is available only in Directional mode. |
| Box3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for the 3D rectangle of the function. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the box along the X-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeY The size of the box along the Y-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. SizeZ The size of the box along the Z-axis of the PointCloud. The value range is 0.001 to inf., and the default value is 100. X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. The value range is -inf. to inf., and the default value is 0. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation of the box (in degrees) about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle of the box (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is 0 <br>- 180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the tilt direction of the box (in degrees) from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, about the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Box is set to 0. Note: This parameter is available only in Directional mode. |
| External Box | Specifies a reference to a Box3D structure defined in another cell of the spreadsheet to be used for plotting. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Box3D structure. Note: This parameter is available only in Directional mode. |
| Minimum Z | Specifies the minimum value of the height color range in Z Range mode. Note: This parameter is available only in Z Range mode. |
| Maximum Z | Specifies the maximum value of the height color range in Z Range mode. Note: This parameter is available only in Z Range mode. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs
