## SortBlob3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/SortBlob3D.htm`*

The SortBlob3D function is used to return a sorted list of the blobs with the largest volume detected in the point cloud, by referencing the spreadsheet cell containing the set of extracted large blobs. The function allows you to sort the referenced blobs by specific sort keys and orders. It returns the list of sorted blobs in a Blobs3D structure, which can be referenced with Blobs3D Vision Data Access functions.

### Inputs

The SortBlob3D function has the following syntax: SortBlob3D(PointCloud,Blobs,SortKey,SortOrder,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Blobs3D | Specifies a reference to a Blobs3D structure in another spreadsheet cell. The contents of this cell will be used as a basis for sorting. |
| Sort Key | Specifies the logic by which the blobs of the referenced Blobs3D structure will be sorted. The available values are the following: <br>- None: No sorting logic will be applied to the list of blobs. Use this setting if you simply want a count of the blobs, or want to examine them without the need to order them. <br>- Volume: Sort the blobs by their volume. Use this setting if you want to examine the blobs sorted by their volume (e.g. from the largest volume to the smallest, or the opposite). This is the default setting. <br>- Bounding Box Size: Sort the blobs by the length of their bounding boxes on the specified axis. Use this setting if you want to examine the blobs sorted by their size (e.g., from the largest to the smallest, or the opposite), with the size specified by the bounding box dimensions of the blobs. This sorting key has four sub-types: <br>- Bounding Box Size X: Sort the blobs by the X-axis length of their bounding boxes. <br>- Bounding Box Size Y: Sort the blobs by the Y-axis length of their bounding boxes. <br>- Bounding Box Size Z: Sort the blobs by the Z-axis length of their bounding boxes. <br>- Bounding Box Size D: Sort the blobs by the diagonal length of their bounding boxes. <br>- Center of Mass: Sort the blobs by their 3D positions in the 3D point cloud. The blob 's 3D position is specified by the location of its center of mass in the point cloud in the specified direction (that is, their X, Y, Z or radial distance from the origin of the specified Sort Reference space). This sorting key has four sub-types: <br>- Center of Mass X: Sort the blobs by the X-axis distance of their center of mass from the origin of the Sort Reference space. <br>- Center of Mass Y: Sort the blobs by the Y-axis distance of their center of mass from the origin of the Sort Reference space. <br>- Center of Mass Z: Sort the blobs by the Z-axis distance of their center of mass from the origin of the Sort Reference space. <br>- Center of Mass R: Sort the blobs by the Euclidean distance of their center of mass from the origin of the Sort Reference space. <br>- Center of Mass Spoke: Sort the blobs by their 2D positions. Use these sort keys, for example, if the objects are arranged in a circular fashion on a plane surface. The "2D position" refers to the blob's center of mass as projected onto the X/Y plane of the Sort Reference's space. This sorting key has two sub-types: <br>- Center of Mass Spoke Angle Norm: Sort the blobs by the normalized spoke angle of their center of mass. <br>- Center of Mass Spoke Angle Abs: Sort the blobs by the absolute spoke angle of their center of mass. <br>- Center of Mass Spoke Radius: Sort the blobs by their center of mass distance from their origin to the center of mass location on the X-axis and Y-axis (disregarding the Z-axis height). <br>- Center of Mass Grid X then Y then Z: Sort by the center-of-mass' X-axis position, then Y-axis position, and finally Z-axis position. <br>- Center of Mass Grid Y then X then Z: Sort by the center-of-mass' Y-axis position, then X-axis position, and finally Z-axis position. |
| Sort Order | Specifies whether to sort the results in ascending or descending order. Note: This parameter is disabled if Sort Key is set to None. |
| Sort Tolerance | Specifies a threshold to determine if 2 or more results are tied. If they are tied, they can be sorted by a subsequent sort. Only takes effect when multiple sorting rules are applied (such as grid sorting or appending a sort tool). Note: This parameter is disabled if Sort Key is set to None. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. Note: This parameter is not available if Sort Key is set to None, Volume, Bounding Box Size X, Bounding Box Size Y, Bounding Box Size Z, or Bounding Box Size D. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. Note: This parameter is not available if Sort Key is set to None, Volume, Bounding Box Size X, Bounding Box Size Y, Bounding Box Size Z, or Bounding Box Size D. |
| Append Sort | When enabled, the selected the sorting rule will be added to the rules inherited from the reference vision or sorting tool. Otherwise, it will override the inherited rules. This setting is enabled by default. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Blobs3D data structure containing the blobs sorted, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

When initially inserted into a cell, the following functions are automatically inserted into the spreadsheet to create a result table.

- **Num Found**：Index
- **Volume**：Height
- **Type**：Bounding Box

| 1 | GetVolume(Blobs3D, 1) |
| GetHeight(Blobs3D, 1) | GetTypeText(Blobs3D, 1) |
| GetBoundingBox(Blobs3D, 1) |... |
|... |... |
|... |... |

| N-1

GetNFound(Blobs3D, index) Returns the number of blobs sorted by the SortBlob3D function. GetTypeText(Blobs3D, index) Returns the blob type of the sorted blob with the specified index. GetVolume(Blobs3D, index) Returns the volume of the sorted blob with the specified index. |

## SortEdge3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/SortEdge3D.htm`*

The SortEdge3D function is used to return a sorted list of edges extracted in the point cloud, by referencing an Edges3D structure (created for example by an ExtractEdge3D function). This function allows you to sort the referenced edges by specific sort keys and sort orders, and returns the list of sorted edges in a new Edges3D structure.

### Inputs

The SortEdge3D function has the following syntax: SortEdge3D(PointCloud,Edges3D,SortKey,SortOrder,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Edges3D | Specifies a reference to an Edges3D structure in another spreadsheet cell. The contents of this cell will be used as the basis for sorting. |
| Sort Key | Specifies the sorting logic for the edges in the Edges3D structure. The available values are the following: <br>- None: No sorting logic will be applied. Use this setting if you simply want to count the sorted edges, or want to examine them without the need to order them. <br>- Score: Sort the edges by their calculated score values. <br>- Coverage: Sort the edges by their coverage amount. <br>- Sharpness: Sort the edges by their sharpness. <br>- Vertical Angle: Sort the edges by their vertical angles. <br>- Horizontal Angle: Sort the edges by their horizontal angles. <br>- Position Along Extraction Direction: Sort the edges by their positions along the direction they were extracted into the Edges3D structure. <br>- Transition Type: Sort the edges by transition type (convex, concave). <br>- Edge Segment Center Spoke Angle: Sort the edges by their angle from the edge segment center's X-axis and Y-axis position to their origin. <br>- Edge Segment Center Spoke Radius: Sort the edges by their segment center's distance from their origin to the segment center's location on the X-axis and Y-axis (disregarding the Z-axis height). |
| Sort Order | Specifies whether to sort the edges of the referenced Edges3D structure in ascending or descending order. Note: This parameter is not available if the Sort Key parameter is set to None. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. Note: This parameter is available only if Sort Key is set to Edge Segment Center Spoke Angle or Edge Segment Center Spoke Radius. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. Note: This parameter is available only if Sort Key is set to Edge Segment Center Spoke Angle or Edge Segment Center Spoke Radius. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

An Edges3D data structure containing the sorted edges, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

|---|---|
|  | GetCoverage(Edges3D, index) Returns the coverage of the edge specified with the index number. GetHorizontalAngle(Edges3D, index) Returns the horizontal angle of the edge specified with the index number. GetLine(Edges3D, index) Returns the line of the extracted edge with the specified index as a Line3D structure. GetMidpoint(Line3D) Returns the midpoint of the specified Line3D structure as a Point3D structure. GetNFound(Edges3D) Returns the number of sorted edges. GetScore(Edges3D, index) Returns the score of the edges specified with the index as a value between 0 and 100. GetSharpness(Edges3D, index) Returns the sharpness of the edge specified with the index (in degrees). GetTransitionTypeText(Edges3D, index) Returns the transition type of the edge specified with the index as a text (convex or concave). GetVerticalAngle(Edges3D, index) Returns the vertical angle of the edge specified with the index number. GetX(Line3D, index) Returns the X-axis coordinate of the specified line's starting point (when using index 0) or endpoint (when using index 1) on the Fixture3D X-axis. GetY(Line3D, index) Returns the Y-axis coordinate of the specified line's starting point (when using index 0) or endpoint (when using index 1) on the Fixture3D Y-axis. GetZ(Line3D, index) Returns the Z-axis coordinate of the specified line's starting point (when using index 0) or endpoint (when using index 1) on the Fixture3D Z-axis. |

## SortPatMax3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/SortPatMax3D.htm`*

The SortPatMax3D function is used to return a sorted list of 3D patterns found by a configured FindPatMax3D function. This function allows you to sort the patterns by specific sort keys and sort orders, and returns the list of sorted patterns in a new Patterns3D structure.

### Inputs

The SortPatMax3D function has the following syntax: SortPlane3D(PointCloud,Patterns3D,SortKey,SortOrder,SortTolerance,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,AppendSort,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Patterns3D | Specifies a reference to a Patterns3D structure in another spreadsheet cell (created typically by a FindPatMax3D function). The contents of this cell will be used as the basis for sorting. |
| Sort Key | Specifies the sorting logic for the patterns in the Patterns3D structure. The available values are the following: <br>- None: No sorting logic will be applied. Use this setting if you simply want to count the sorted patterns, or want to examine them without the need to order them. <br>- Score: Sort the patterns by their calculated score values. <br>- Pose Rotation In-Plane Rotation Angle Norm: Sort by the pose rotation's norm in-plane rotation. <br>- Pose Rotation In-Plane Rotation Angle Abs: Sort by the pose rotation's absolute in-plane rotation. <br>- Pose Rotation Tilt Direction Norm: Sort by the pose rotation's norm tilt direction. <br>- Pose Rotation Tilt Direction Abs: Sort by the pose rotation's absolute tilt direction. <br>- Pose Rotation Tilt Angle: Sort by the pose rotation's tilt angle. <br>- Pose Translation X: Sort by the pose translation's X-component. <br>- Pose Translation Y: Sort by the pose translation's Y-component. <br>- Pose Translation Z: Sort by the pose translation's Z-component. <br>- Pose Translation R: Sort by the pose translation's Euclidean distance. <br>- Pose Translation Spoke Angle Norm: Sort by the pose translation's norm spoke angle. <br>- Pose Translation Spoke Angle Abs: Sort by the pose translation's absolute spoke angle. <br>- Pose Translation Spoke Radius: Sort by the pose translation's spoke radius. <br>- Pose Translation X then Y then Z: Sort by the pose translation's Grid X then Y, and then Z. <br>- Pose Translation Y then X then Z: Sort by the pose translation's Grid X then Y, and then Z. |
| Sort Order | Specifies whether to sort the patterns of the referenced Patterns3D structure in ascending or descending order. Note: This parameter is not available if Sort Key is set to None. |
| Sort Tolerance | Specifies a threshold to determine if 2 or more results are tied. If they are tied, they can be sorted by a subsequent sort. Only takes effect when multiple sorting rules are applied (such as grid sorting or appending a sort tool). Note: This parameter is disabled if Sort Key is set to None. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. Note: This parameter is not available if Sort Key is set to None or Score. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. Note: This parameter is not available if Sort Key is set to None or Score. |
| Append Sort | When enabled, the selected the sorting rule will be added to the rules inherited from the reference vision or sorting tool. Otherwise, it will override the inherited rules. This setting is enabled by default. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Patterns3D data structure containing the sorted planes, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

## SortPlane3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/SortPlane3D.htm`*

The SortPlane3D function is used to return a sorted list of planes extracted in the point cloud, by referencing a Planes3D structure (created for example by an ExtractPlane3D function). This function allows you to sort the referenced planes by specific sort keys and sort orders, and returns the list of sorted planes in a new Planes3D structure.

### Inputs

The SortPlane3D function has the following syntax: SortPlane3D(PointCloud,Planes3D,SortKey,SortOrder,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,ResultGraphic,Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Planes3D | Specifies a reference to an Planes3D structure in another spreadsheet cell. The contents of this cell will be used as the basis for sorting. |
| Sort Key | Specifies the sorting logic for the planes in the Planes3D structure. The available values are the following: <br>- None: No sorting logic will be applied. Use this setting if you simply want to count the sorted planes, or want to examine them without the need to order them. <br>- Score: Sort the planes by their calculated score values. <br>- Number of Inliers: Sort the planes by their number of inliers. <br>- Residuals RMS: Sort the planes by the root mean square of their residuals. <br>- Residuals Max: Sort the planes by their maximum residuals. <br>- Inlier Density Over Rectangle: Sort the planes by the density of their inliers over their rectangles. <br>- Area of Rectangle: Sort the planes by the area of their finite rectangles. <br>- Relative Pitch: Sort the planes by their relative pitches. <br>- Center of Rectangle X: Sort the planes by the X-axis distance of their rectangle's center point from the origin of the point cloud space. <br>- Center of Rectangle Y: Sort the planes by the Y-axis distance of their rectangle's center point from the origin of the point cloud space. <br>- Center of Rectangle Z: Sort the planes by the Z-axis distance of their rectangle's center point from the origin of the point cloud space. <br>- Center of Rectangle R: Sort the planes by the radial distance of their rectangle's center point from the origin of the point cloud space. <br>- Center of Rectangle Spoke Angle: Sort the planes by their angle from their rectangle's center's X-axis and Y-axis position to their origin. <br>- Center of Rectangle Spoke Radius: Sort the planes by the center of their rectangle's distance from their origin to the center of their patch's location on the X-axis and Y-axis (disregarding the Z-axis height). |
| Sort Order | Specifies whether to sort the planes of the referenced Planes3D structure in ascending or descending order. Note: This parameter is not available if the Sort Key parameter is set to None. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. Note: This parameter is only available if Sort Key is set to Center of Patch X, Center of Patch Y, Center of Patch Z, Center of Patch R, Center of Patch Spoke Angle, or Center of Patch Spoke Radius. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. Note: This parameter is only available if Sort Key is set to Center of Patch X, Center of Patch Y, Center of Patch Z, Center of Patch R, Center of Patch Spoke Angle, or Center of Patch Spoke Radius. |
| Result Graphics | Selects the type of graphics to use for showing the results: <br>- 0 = Surface (default) <br>- 1 = Plane |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

A Planes3D data structure containing the sorted planes, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

## Sphere3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/Sphere3D.htm`*

The Sphere3D function allows you to create a fixtured 3D sphere in the point cloud. It returns a Sphere3D structure containing the settings of the fixtured sphere.

### Inputs

The Sphere3D function has the following syntax: Sphere3D(PointCloud,Fixture3D,ExternalFixture,Sphere3D,Show)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Sphere3D | Specifies the radius and location of the 3D sphere. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {Radius, X, Y, Z} Radius The radius of the 3D sphere. The value range is 0.001 to inf. X Offset of the center point of the 3D sphere on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Y Offset of the center point of the 3D sphere on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Z Offset of the center point of the 3D sphere on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. The value range is -inf. to inf. Show Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics will be hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input graphics only | The input data will be displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Sphere3D structure containing the parameters of the configured sphere, or #ERR if any parameter has been configured incorrectly.

- **Radius**：X
- **Y**：Z

## TrainPatMax3D

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/TrainPatMax3D.htm`*

The TrainPatMax3D function is used to extract and train a 3D pattern in the point cloud. This pattern is then used with the FindPatMax3D function. The function returns a Model3D structure.

## TrainPatMax3D Overview

The TrainPatMax3D function is used to extract and train a 3D pattern in the point cloud. This pattern is then used with the FindPatMax3D function.

### Inputs

The TrainPatMax3D function has the following syntax: TrainPatMax3D(PointCloud, Fixture3D, ExternalFixture, Box3D, ExternalRegion, ExcludeBasePlane, Plane3D, ExternalPlane, PatternOrigin, PatMax3DVersion, FeatureSize, TrainEvent, Timeout, Show) See the table for a description of the available parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 = result graphics only | The result graphics of the function are displayed at all times. |
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Fixture3D | Specifies the point cloud coordinate system in which the 3D fixture is defined. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the PointCloud Z-axis after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated PointCloud X-axis of the tool, around the PointCloud Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -180 to 180. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: The Fixture3D parameter is only available if you set External Fixture to 0. Note: You can use the Fixture3D parameter to set the ROI fixture. |
| External Fixture | Specifies a reference to a Fixture3D structure defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the fixture of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal fixture of the function instead. |
| Box3D | Specifies the dimensions, offset and angle for 3D region of interest (ROI) of the function. It is offset from the Fixture3D origin in the following format with the following arguments: {SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ, X, Y, Z, Rotation, Tilt, TiltDirection} SizeX The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D X-axis. SizeY The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Y-axis. SizeZ The size of the ROI along the Fixture3D Z-axis. X Offset on the X-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the Fixture3D origin. Rotation Specifies the in-plane rotation in degrees around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle in degrees from the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool after rotation. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt in degrees from the rotated Fixture3D X-axis of the tool, around the Fixture3D Z-axis of the tool. The value range is -360 to 360. The tool normalizes external references with values outside the allowed range to the allowed range. Note: This setting is only available if you set External Region to 0. |
| External Region | Specifies a reference to a 3D region defined in another cell. The function uses the referenced cell as the Region of Interest of the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the internal Box3D structure of the function as the ROI. |
| Exclude Base Plane | When enabled, the function adds a separate planar region of interest (ROI), so that the surface plane can be excluded when training or finding a 3D pattern, improving the performance of the tool. This setting is disabled by default, as undesired areas can also be excluded with appropriate placement of the Box3D structure. |
| Plane3D | Specifies the offset and the angle of the plane to use. It is offset from the PointCloud origin in the following format with the following arguments: {X, Y, Z, Tilt, TiltDirection} X Offset on the X-axis from the PointCloud origin. Y Offset on the Y-axis from the PointCloud origin. Z Offset on the Z-axis from the PointCloud origin. Tilt Specifies the tilt angle (in degrees) from the PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the direction of tilt (in degrees) from the plane's rotated PointCloud X-axis, about the tool's PointCloud Z-axis. The value range is -360 <br>- 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Note: This parameter is available only if External Plane is set to 0. Note: You can use Plane3D to mask data for training. The Plane3D function prevents the tool from taking any points that belong to that plane and are within the ROI. Note: This parameter is available only if Exclude Base Plane is True and External Plane is 0. |
| External Plane | Specifies a reference to a Rectangle3D or Circle3D structure defined in another cell to be used by the function. Set to 0 (OFF) to use the function's internal Plane3D structure instead. Note: This parameter is available only if Exclude Base Plane is True. |
| Pattern Origin | Specifies the X, Y and Z-axis location of the training pattern's origin, as offsets from the center of the training region. |
| Offset X | Specifies the X-axis offset from the center of the trained pattern. |
| Offset Y | Specifies the Y-axis offset from the center of the trained pattern. |
| Offset Z | Specifies the Z-axis offset from the center of the trained pattern. Rotation Specifies the training pattern's in-plane rotation (in degrees) about the Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. Tilt Specifies the training pattern's tilt angle (in degrees) from the Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is 0-180. External references with values outside the allowed range will result in an error. Tilt Direction Specifies the training pattern's direction of tilt (in degrees) from the tool's rotated Fixture3D X-axis, about the tool's Fixture3D Z-axis. The value range is -360 to 360. External references with values outside the allowed range will be normalized to the allowed range. PatMax3D Version <br>- 1.0 (1) <br>- use for existing jobs to ensure that results remain consistent. <br>- 2.0 (2) <br>- returns pose results twice as fast on average. Recommended for new jobs. Note: The accuracy of the two versions is generally equal. However, there can be cases where one PatMax3D version produces a result, but the other does not. |
| Feature Size | Specifies the sampling quality of the point cloud points and patches that PatMax3D will use for alignment. The available values are the following: <br>- 0 = Large: Calculate alignment using large features. <br>- 1 = Medium: Calculate alignment using medium features. This is the default setting. <br>- 2 = Small: Calculate alignment using small features. Tip: <br>- Lower values (Large and Medium) increase alignment performance, but are less accurate. <br>- The Small value results in more accurate alignment and better noise data sensitivity, at the cost of performance. Train Event Trains the configured pattern upon clicking the button. Timeout Specifies a length of time (in milliseconds) to allow the training to run. The function execution stops if the time out exceeds the configured value. |
| Show | Selects the type of graphics to overlay on the image. |
| 0 = hide all (default) | All graphics are hidden, except when the cell containing the function is highlighted in the spreadsheet. |
| 2 = input and result graphics | The region of interest, the input data and the results are displayed at all times. |

### Outputs

Returns

A Model3D data structure containing the trained pattern, or #ERR if any of the input parameters are invalid.

Results

Trained

| Function | Description |

The function returns 1 if it does, and 0 if it does not. GetX(Point3D) Returns the X-axis coordinate of the model's origin point. GetY(Point3D) Returns the Y-axis coordinate of the model's origin point. GetZ(Point3D) Returns the Z-axis coordinate of the model's origin point. |

## WritePointCloud

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/WritePointCloud.htm`*

The WritePointCloud function is used to save the acquired point cloud acquisitions into Filmstrip files, even when the vision system is Online. The function lets you save the acquired point cloud data onto:

- The internal storage of the vision system
- A remote FTP server
- A remote SFTP server You can load the saved point cloud data into the Filmstrip with the appropriate Filmstrip controls.

### Inputs

The WritePointCloud function has the following syntax: WritePointCloud(PointCloud,Event,Storage,Server,UserName,Password,FilePath,FileName,AppendMode,MaxAppendValue,Reset)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PointCloud | Reference to a cell containing a point cloud. The default value is $A$0. |
| Event | Specifies an external event forcing In-Sight Spreadsheet to save the acquired point cloud. This can be an Event structure or a Button function. Tip: If no changes are made to this parameter, the function automatically creates and references a WriteButton on the spreadsheet. |
| Storage | Specifies the storage where the saved point clouds are stored: <br>- Local Device: The acquired point cloud data is saved to the internal storage of the vision system. <br>- FTP Server: The acquired point cloud data is saved onto the specified remote FTP storage. This is the default setting. <br>- SFTP Server: The acquired point cloud data is saved onto the specified remote SFTP storage. |
| Server | Specifies the valid IP address of the FTP server in an IPAddress:PortNumber format (e.g. 99.99.99.99:1234). Note: This parameter is enabled only if Storage is set to FTP Server or SFTP Server. |
| User Name | Specifies a valid login username for the FTP server. Note: This parameter is enabled only if Storage is set to FTP Server or SFTP Server. |
| Password | Specifies a valid login password for the FTP server. Note: This parameter is enabled only if Storage is set to FTP Server or SFTP Server. |
| File Path | Specifies the location where the point cloud data will be saved. Note: <br>- When saving data to the vision system's internal storage, this parameter defaults to the device's root directory. <br>- When saving data to an FTP server or SFTP server, provide the full path of the directory. |
| File Name | Specifies the file name of the saved point cloud data. The specified suffix (configured with Append Mode) will be appended to this file name for all saved point cloud data file. Tip: Do not specify the file extension. |
| Append Mode | Specifies the type of information appended to the file name when saving point cloud data: <br>- Index: The function will append the acquisition index number to the file name. This is the default setting. <br>- Timestamp: The function will append the acquisition timestamp to the file name. |
| Max. Append Value | Specifies the highest index value that the function can append to the file name. Once this value is reached, the index numbering will restart with the next acquisition, overwriting the saved files with the same name. Note: <br>- The value range is 0 <br>- 9999999. Specifying a value outside this range (such as -1) will result in no suffixes appended to the file names. <br>- This parameter is enabled only if Append Mode is set to Index. |
| Reset | When enabled, it resets point cloud writing at the next Event. Tip: If no changes are made to this parameter, the function will automatically create and reference a ResetButton on the spreadsheet. |

### Outputs

Returns

A ❒WritePointCloud function, along with a default set of Write and Reset buttons (if using the default values of the Event and Reset parameters).

Results

Once inserted into a cell with the default settings, click the Write button to save the currently acquired point cloud, or click Reset to reset the save event.

Description

Returns the transition type of the specified 3D circle (1 = convex; 2 = concave).

## Unit Conversions

*源文件：`3DVisionTools/unit-conversions.htm`*

When using the In-Sight L38, you need to convert some units while working with multiple 2D/3D tools. The values you enter a 2D tool must be in pixels and in the correct coordinate system. Example:

- 3D Tool:
- Input: Real world units (right-handed coordinate system) - Output: Real world units
- 2D Tool:
- Input: Pixels (left-handed coordinate system) - Output: Real world units Note: This conversion is applicable only on specific 2D outputs, like the gray scale (intensity) image. Moving from a 2D tool to a 3D one does not require any conversions. You need to go through this procedure only when using two 2D tools subsequently, or switching from 3D to 2D. The exact steps are described in the following subsections:
